items.titleEn: Blue Jays have golden opportunity to tighten Wild Card race with Guardians
bodyEn: After a vintage Max Scherzer performance punctuated a three-game sweep of the Mariners this past weekend, the Blue Jays -- through all the adversity they’ve faced this season -- sit just 1 1/2 games back of the third American League Wild Card spot.
And they have a premium chance to close that gap this week.
The Blue Jays begin a three-game set against the Guardians -- the team currently holding that third Wild Card slot -- on Tuesday at Progressive Field.

It’s perhaps the biggest series of the season for Toronto to date, and the club has planned accordingly. Manager John Schneider used Monday’s off-day to make sure AL Cy Young contender Dylan Cease and José Soriano will pitch in the series on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively. Spencer Arrighetti is scheduled to throw on Tuesday, with Spencer Miles as an opener.

Across from that Toronto trio will be Cleveland’s Gavin Williams on Tuesday, Joey Cantillo on Wednesday and a to-be-announced starter on Thursday. Tuesday and Wednesday are night games with first pitch scheduled for 6:40 p.m. ET, while Thursday is a day game at 1:10 p.m. ET.
Here are three storylines to watch entering the series.
1. Tie it down

Beyond the straightforward importance of beating the team in front of you in the standings, the Blue Jays also enter with a 2-1 advantage over the Guardians in the season series. Clinching the season set would give Toronto the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland, should it be necessary in determining playoff position.

Furthermore, the Blue Jays are in pole position entering September against four of the six teams which are primary threats to the final Wild Card spot. They are 2-1 against the Guardians with three games remaining; 4-3 against the Orioles with six games remaining; 4-2 against the Mariners with no games remaining; and 2-1 against the Tigers with three games remaining.
The Blue Jays only trail the Twins (3-4 with no remaining games) and the Rangers (0-4 with three games left).
If Toronto were to end the season tied with any of those teams for the final postseason berth, the head-to-head record would be the first tiebreaker, followed by intra-division record.
Swingin’ it
The Blue Jays’ 17-11 August -- their best month in 2026 -- was fueled not only by Cease’s continued excellence (2.03 ERA in five starts) but also by three key offensive performances.

Alejandro Kirk posted a 160 wRC+ -- a metric that measures overall offensive production on a 100-point scale -- that would make him the 14th-best hitter in MLB in August. George Springer finished the month at 25th with a 141 wRC+, while Trade Deadline addition Brett Bateman was 51st with a 127 wRC+.

After missing a large chunk of the season with a left thumb fracture, Kirk looked more like himself in August, hitting .341 with five home runs, 20 RBIs and more walks (12) than strikeouts (nine). The catcher was held hitless just three times in the 22 games he started, while he posted multiple hits seven times.

Springer shook off a slow start to the season and has been excellent in the second half. After going 7-for-11 with four extra-base hits in three games against the Mariners, the 36-year-old’s post-All-Star Game OPS is up to .892.

Meanwhile, Bateman -- after making his Major League debut on Aug. 7 -- has hit in 15 of his first 19 games. Acquired in the Kevin Gausman trade with the Cubs, the outfielder has taken over the Blue Jays’ leadoff spot and has reached base at a strong .384 mark.
Can he get going?

Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s surprisingly down season has been well-documented, as he's still awaiting his first home run at Rogers Center since ... last season. He also hit one home run in August while slashing .221/.259/.312 -- good for just a 59 wRC+.

It’s clear that Guerrero has not been “right” all season, and he missed some time this past month with a concussion. But he has the support of his manager, and if Vladdy can put together even a mini hot streak in the season’s final month, it could do wonders for the Blue Jays’ final push toward October.

items.titleEn: Beloved 'Voice of the Expos' Doucet dies at 86
bodyEn: Jacques Doucet, known as the “Voice of the Expos”, died at 86 last week, his daughter Martine confirmed on social media. Doucet spent 33 years as the beloved French language play-by-play broadcaster for the Expos and served as a pivotal figure in popularizing the French vocabulary used to describe baseball.

A cause of death was not disclosed, but Doucet revealed in 2024 that he was battling Alzheimer’s disease. The Blue Jays honored him with a moment of silence before last Friday’s game against the Mariners.

“We join the MLB community and our colleagues at TVA Sports in extending our sincere condolences to the family and friends of Jacques Doucet,” the Blue Jays wrote in a statement. “The ‘Voice of Baseball’ in Quebec and a Canadian Baseball Hall of Famer - his impact on the game and the Montreal Expos will be remembered forever.”

Born in Montreal in 1940, Doucet got his start as a sports journalist with The Canadian Press and later covered the Expos' first years for La Presse. He became the club’s full-time French-language radio voice in 1972 and stayed in the role until the franchise left to become the Washington Nationals following the 2004 season.

Doucet then called independent league games for the Quebec Capitales, a member of the Can-Am League, from 2006 until 2011. An opportunity to return to the Major Leagues arose, and Doucet continued his career as the French broadcaster of Blue Jays games from 2011 until his retirement in 2022.

Among more than 5,500 MLB broadcasts, Doucet was on hand for the Expos’ 1981 NLCS run and two perfect games: Dennis Martinez in 1991, for the Expos against the Dodgers, and David Cone in 1999, for the Yankees against the Expos. He also provided French-language broadcasts for World Series games from 1982 through 1999.

Doucet additionally wrote several books, including “Les Secrets du baseball” with former Major League pitcher Claude Raymond and “Il était une fois les Expos,” a history of the franchise co-written with Marc Robitaille.

Doucet’s illustrious career featured an induction to the Expos’ Hall of Fame in 2003, the Quebec Baseball Hall of Fame in 2002 and the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame in 2020. He also received the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame’s Jack Graney Award in 2004 and was a finalist for the National Baseball Hall of Fame’s Ford C. Frick Award on multiple occasions.
items.titleZh: '博览会之声' Doucet 去世，享年86岁
items.summaryZh: '博览会之声' Doucet 去世，享年86岁，曾为博览会队和蓝鸟队担任法语解说。
bodyZh: 被誉为“博览会之声”的 Jacques Doucet 上周去世，享年86岁，他的女儿 Martine 在社交媒体上证实了这一消息。Doucet 曾担任博览会队深受喜爱的法语实况解说员长达33年，并在推广描述棒球的法语词汇方面发挥了关键作用。
死因尚未公布，但 Doucet 在2024年透露自己正在与阿尔茨海默病作斗争。蓝鸟队在上周五对阵水手队的比赛前为他默哀片刻。
蓝鸟队在一份声明中写道：“我们与 MLB 大家庭以及 TVA Sports 的同事们一起，向 Jacques Doucet 的家人和朋友致以诚挚的哀悼。他是魁北克的‘棒球之声’，也是加拿大棒球名人堂成员——他对这项运动和蒙特利尔博览会队的影响将被永远铭记。”
Doucet 于1940年出生于蒙特利尔，最初在加拿大通讯社担任体育记者，后来为《La Presse》报道了博览会队最初的几个赛季。1972年，他成为该俱乐部法语电台的专职解说员，直到2004赛季结束后球队迁往华盛顿成为华盛顿国民队。
此后，Doucet 于2006年至2011年担任独立联盟球队魁北克首都队（Can-Am 联盟成员）的比赛解说。后来出现了重返大联盟的机会，Doucet 于2011年起担任蓝鸟队比赛的法语解说，直至2022年退休。
在超过5500场 MLB 转播中，Doucet 参与了博览会队1981年国联冠军赛的征程，以及两场完全比赛：1991年 Dennis Martinez 代表博览会队对阵道奇队，以及1999年 David Cone 代表洋基队对阵博览会队。他还于1982年至1999年期间为世界大赛提供法语转播。
此外，Doucet 还写了几本书，包括与前大联盟投手 Claude Raymond 合著的《Les Secrets du baseball》，以及与 Marc Robitaille 合著的队史《Il était une fois les Expos》。
Doucet 辉煌的职业生涯包括2003年入选博览会队名人堂、2002年入选魁北克棒球名人堂以及2020年入选加拿大棒球名人堂。他还于2004年获得加拿大棒球名人堂的 Jack Graney 奖，并多次入围国家棒球名人堂的 Ford C. Frick 奖最终名单。

items.titleEn: Which franchise legend could be next to join Blue Jays' Hall of Excellence?
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Across the many renovations that have modernized Rogers Centre, some of the most important changes the Blue Jays have made look to the past.

First came the nods to history along the 100 level, where the pillars now hold displays with memorabilia from 50 seasons of Blue Jays baseball. Then came the back-to-back World Series statue in front of the stadium, that famous image of Joe Carter. This past weekend brought the main attraction, though, when the Blue Jays opened their Hall of Excellence and inducted the great Buck Martinez, who joined the 11 existing members.

Five years ago, the Blue Jays had the Level of Excellence wrapped around the facing of the 400 level, but the club’s history wasn’t accessible enough. Young fans, or even fans in their 20s and 30s, weren’t hearing the stories of Dave Stieb, George Bell and those great teams of the 1980s often enough. That’s changed.

“The Hall of Excellence creates a permanent home for the stories, achievement and memories of the players and leaders who helped build this franchise and shape Blue Jays history,” said club president and CEO Mark Shapiro at the unveiling. “The individuals represented here established the foundation of this organization and we are proud to ensure that their stories will continue to be told for years to come.”

This also included a call for fans to be part of the process moving forward, with voting now open on the club’s website. Along with a write-in option, the names suggested are: Devon White, Edwin Encarnación, Ernie Whitt, Fred McGriff, Tom Henke, Jimmy Key, John Olerud, Pat Hentgen, Lloyd Moseby, Jesse Barfield, Vernon Wells, Juan Guzmán, Jim Clancy and Duane Ward.
With a clear intent to grow this space, it begs the question: Who’s next?
LHP Jimmy Key (1984-1992)
When you get past franchise icons Stieb and Roy Halladay, who will share the tops of these franchise leaderboards forever, you start running into Key’s name an awful lot.

His 3.42 ERA with the Blue Jays is tied with Stieb -- and just 0.01 runs better than Halladay -- over 1,695 2/3 innings. Key and Stieb led so many of those great rotations through the mid- and late 80s, Key the lefty who was always under control, Stieb the fiery right-hander. Beyond Stieb and Halladay, only Clancy has thrown more innings in a Blue Jays uniform than Key.
RHP Tom Henke (1985-1992)

The greatest closer in Blue Jays history, Henke and the late Ward formed a back end that feels decades ahead of its time in hindsight. Henke’s 217 saves tower above the rest, with Ward’s 121 the closest in second place.

Henke’s case runs up against what so many others do, which is that we’re talking about tenures of six or eight years, not 10 or 12, which could be the tipping point. The importance of Henke’s addition prior to the 1985 season can never be overstated, though, and the role he played in taking the young Blue Jays organization to another level must always be remembered.
DH Edwin Encarnación (2009-2016)

Once again, if Encarnación had played a few more seasons in Toronto, this case would be undeniable. His run from 2012-16 was remarkable, though, forming one of the most feared one-two punches in baseball alongside José Bautista.

Encarnación works as an interesting debate alongside Vernon Wells and Josh Donaldson, and there’s no wrong answer here. Do you prefer a player who was truly elite in a short time like Donaldson, a player who was very good over the medium term like Encarnación, or a player who was solid for parts of 12 seasons in Toronto and climbed plenty of all-time leaderboards like Wells?
Broadcaster Jerry Howarth
The radio voice of the Blue Jays for 36 seasons, Howarth brought us so much of this organization’s history right alongside Tom Cheek, who he could someday join again in the Hall of Excellence.

Martinez was recently inducted under the “Builders and Broadcasters” designation, which also applies to Cheek, Paul Beeston and Pat Gillick. The Blue Jays have a rich media history that stretches into the press box, including the Hall of Famer Bob Elliott and Alison Gordon, who in 1979 became the first woman to cover an MLB beat full-time for the Toronto Star.

Broadcasters welcome fans into the game every night, though, like Dan Shulman and Joe Siddall do now. For 36 years, Blue Jays fans turned on their radio and heard that familiar voice of Howarth welcoming them … “Hello, friends!”
items.titleZh: 下一位加入蓝鸟卓越名人堂的球队传奇是谁？
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟卓越名人堂候选名单公布，谁将是下一位入选的传奇？
bodyZh: 多伦多——在让 Rogers Centre 现代化的多次翻新中，蓝鸟队所做的一些最重要改变却着眼于过去。
首先是在100层看台对历史的致敬，那里的柱子上现在陈列着蓝鸟队50个赛季的纪念品。然后是体育场前的背靠背世界大赛雕像，那是 Joe Carter 的著名形象。不过，上周末迎来了重头戏，蓝鸟队开启了他们的卓越名人堂，并入选了伟大的 Buck Martinez，他加入了现有的11位成员。
五年前，蓝鸟队的“卓越层”环绕在400层看台的正面，但球队的历史还不够亲近。年轻球迷，甚至二十多岁和三十多岁的球迷，并不经常听到 Dave Stieb、George Bell 以及那些1980年代伟大球队的故事。如今这已经改变。
俱乐部主席兼首席执行官 Mark Shapiro 在揭幕仪式上表示：“卓越名人堂为那些帮助建立这支球队、塑造蓝鸟历史的球员和领袖的故事、成就和回忆提供了一个永久的家。这里所代表的个人奠定了这支球队的基础，我们很自豪能够确保他们的故事在未来多年继续被讲述。”

这还包括呼吁球迷参与未来的评选过程，俱乐部网站上的投票现已开放。除了手写选项外，建议的名字还有：Devon White、Edwin Encarnación、Ernie Whitt、Fred McGriff、Tom Henke、Jimmy Key、John Olerud、Pat Hentgen、Lloyd Moseby、Jesse Barfield、Vernon Wells、Juan Guzmán、Jim Clancy 和 Duane Ward。
怀着明确扩展这一空间的意图，问题随之而来：下一位是谁？
左投手 Jimmy Key（1984-1992）
当你越过球队偶像 Stieb 和 Roy Halladay——他们将永远占据球队历史榜单的顶端——你会开始频繁看到 Key 的名字。
他在蓝鸟队的自责分率为3.42，与 Stieb 持平，比 Halladay 低0.01分，投了1695又2/3局。Key 和 Stieb 在80年代中后期领衔了众多伟大的先发轮值，Key 是永远掌控局面的左投手，Stieb 是火热的右投手。在 Stieb 和 Halladay 之外，只有 Clancy 身披蓝鸟战袍的投球局数超过 Key。
右投手 Tom Henke（1985-1992）
作为蓝鸟队历史上最伟大的终结者，Henke 与已故的 Ward 组成的后援组合，事后看来领先于那个时代数十年。Henke 的217次救援成功高居队史之首，Ward 的121次紧随其后位列第二。
Henke 的案例与许多其他人一样，我们谈论的是六或八年的任期，而不是十年或十二年，这可能是决定性因素。然而，Henke 在1985赛季前加盟的重要性怎么强调都不为过，他在将年轻的蓝鸟队提升到另一个层次中所扮演的角色必须永远被铭记。
指定打击 Edwin Encarnación（2009-2016）
再一次，如果 Encarnación 在多伦多多打几个赛季，他的入选将无可争议。不过，他在2012-16赛季的表现非常出色，与 José Bautista 组成了棒球界最令人生畏的双人组合之一。
Encarnación 与 Vernon Wells 和 Josh Donaldson 构成了一个有趣的辩论，这里没有错误答案。你更喜欢像 Donaldson 那样在短时间内真正精英的球员，像 Encarnación 那样在中期内表现出色的球员，还是像 Wells 那样在多伦多效力12个赛季且在大量历史榜单中攀升的稳健球员？
解说员 Jerry Howarth
作为蓝鸟队36个赛季的电台之声，Howarth 与 Tom Cheek 一起为我们带来了这支球队的众多历史，他或许有一天能再次在卓越名人堂中与 Cheek 相聚。
Martinez 最近以“建设者与解说员”的身份入选，这一类别也适用于 Cheek、Paul Beeston 和 Pat Gillick。蓝鸟队有着丰富的媒体历史，延伸到记者席，包括名人堂成员 Bob Elliott 和 Alison Gordon，后者在1979年成为首位全职为《多伦多星报》报道 MLB 球队的女性。
不过，解说员每晚都欢迎球迷进入比赛，就像现在 Dan Shulman 和 Joe Siddall 所做的那样。36年来，蓝鸟球迷打开收音机，听到 Howarth 那熟悉的声音欢迎他们……“朋友们，你们好！”

items.titleEn: Mad Max makes more history, strikes out 10 to pass Perry for 9th all-time
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Max Scherzer climbed another rung of the all-time Major League Baseball strikeouts ladder in the Blue Jays’ 7-0 win over the Mariners on Sunday.
With his seventh-inning punch out of Cal Raleigh, his 10th of the game, Scherzer surpassed Gaylord Perry for ninth all-time with 3,535 strikeouts.
When it was announced to the Rogers Centre crowd, fans erupted in appreciation for the history they were witnessing. In typical Scherzer fashion, he saluted the crowd before getting back to work.

It was the 115th time in Scherzer’s illustrious career that he had struck out at least 10 batters in a game. He is third in that category, behind only Nolan Ryan (215) and Randy Johnson (212) since the mound moved to its current distance in 1893.
Every member of the 3,000-strikeout club

At 42 years and 34 days old, Scherzer is also the oldest pitcher with 10+ strikeouts and one or no hits allowed in a game since Ryan on May 1, 1991, (44 years, 90 days) in a no-hitter against none other than the Blue Jays.
Scherzer and Ryan (six times) are the only pitchers with such an outing at age 42+ in MLB history.

After Josh Naylor grounded out to second base to end the seventh, Scherzer walked off the mound with a 4-0 lead and a standing ovation from the Jays faithful. Scherzer threw 67 of his 97 pitches for strikes, with one walk and Raleigh's fourth-inning double the only baserunners he allowed.
items.titleZh: Mad Max再创历史，单场10K超越Perry升至历史第9位
items.summaryZh: Scherzer单场10次三振，生涯3535K超越Perry，升至历史第9位。
bodyZh: 多伦多——Max Scherzer在周日蓝鸟7-0战胜水手的比赛中，在大联盟历史三振榜上又登上了一级台阶。
凭借第七局对Cal Raleigh投出的三振，也是本场比赛的第10次三振，Scherzer以3535次三振超越Gaylord Perry，升至历史第九位。
当这一消息在罗杰斯中心球场宣布时，现场球迷爆发出欢呼，感谢他们正在见证历史。Scherzer以他一贯的方式向人群致意，然后重新投入比赛。
这是Scherzer辉煌职业生涯中第115次在单场比赛中三振至少10名打者。自1893年投手丘移到目前距离以来，他在这项数据上排名第三，仅次于Nolan Ryan（215次）和Randy Johnson（212次）。
3000次三振俱乐部的每一位成员
在42岁零34天的时候，Scherzer也成为自1991年5月1日Ryan在对阵蓝鸟的比赛中投出无安打（44岁零90天）以来，单场三振10次以上且最多只被击出一支安打的年龄最大的投手。
在大联盟历史上，Scherzer和Ryan（6次）是仅有的在42岁及以上还曾做到单场10K且最多被打1安的投手。
当Josh Naylor在第七局击出二垒方向滚地球出局后，Scherzer带着4-0的领先优势走下投手丘，全场蓝鸟球迷起立鼓掌。Scherzer共投97球，其中67球为好球，仅投出一次保送，另有Raleigh在第四局击出的二垒安打，这是对手仅有的两次上垒。

items.titleEn: Jays' top pitching prospect helps Double-A squad to latest bit of delicious history
bodyEn: Unique happenings are often afoot when the Double-A New Hampshire Fisher Cats dip into their alternate identity bag and step out as the Manchester Chicken Tenders.

On June 7, 2025, Rafael Sanchez spun a seven-inning no-hitter when the team took the field as the Buffalo Tenders, a spicy offshoot. Incredibly, they were back at it again April 28 when four Fisher Cats hurlers combined to toss yet another no-no while under the guise of the Chicken Tenders.

So when Nolan Perry, the Blue Jays’ No. 2 prospect, toed the slab Saturday night, it was a precursor that something special could happen. Add in that it was the second time ever the club was donning their latest offshoot -- the Coconut Tenders -- and it all came together for a perfectly delicious blend of history during the club’s 6-4 loss to Hartford at Delta Dental Stadium.
Get tickets to a Minor League game near you »

Perry lost the no-hit bid right out of the chute, so the Tenders would have to find an even sweeter way to make history. The 2026 All-Star Futures Game representative racked up a pair of strikeouts in both the first and second, then notched a fifth in the third, before adding two more in the fourth, marking his eighth start this season with at least seven punchouts to his credit.

But when the bullpen door swung open, batters kept on swinging and missing. Righty Alex Amalfi notched five strikeouts in two frames. Gage Stanifer (TOR No. 10) notched all six of his outs by way of the K before Yondrei Rojas added two punchouts of his own. All told, the Fisher Cats’ pitching staff finished with 20 strikeouts, the most in franchise history.

Perry topped out at 75 pitches as Toronto continues to keep a close eye on his workload in his first season back from Tommy John surgery. He’s already up to a career-high 73 2/3 innings this year and missed a chunk of time after taking a line drive off the head. But when healthy, he’s backed up being ranked No. 95 overall by MLB Pipeline with a 2.81 ERA, .196 average against and 12.6 K/9 across three levels.

Stanifer first pitched out of relief this season back on Aug. 6 and has since made seven appearances as a multi-inning reliever. He’s racked up 22 strikeouts over 14 innings in that span and held opposing batters to a .184 average. Equipped with one of the most wicked one-two punches of offerings in the Jays’ system with his fastball/slider combo, Stanifer has shown an ability to continue missing bats in his new role.

The addition of the Coconut Tenders to the alt identity family was meant to bring a bit of sweet summer vibes to the Granite State. But it’s also provided the Fisher Cats with a little extra flavor as they make history.

bodyZh: 当2A新罕布什尔费舍猫队（New Hampshire Fisher Cats）从他们的替补身份包中拿出另一个身份，以曼彻斯特鸡柳队（Manchester Chicken Tenders）出场时，独特的事情往往会发生。

因此，当蓝鸟队2号潜力新秀Nolan Perry周六晚上踏上投手丘时，这预示着可能会发生一些特别的事情。再加上这是球队第二次穿上最新分支身份“椰子鸡柳”（Coconut Tenders），这一切汇聚成了一段完美而美味的历史，尽管球队在Delta Dental球场以6比4输给了Hartford。

Perry 一开始就失去了无安打比赛的希望，因此鸡柳队需要找到一种更甜蜜的方式来创造历史。这位2026年全明星未来之星赛代表在第一局和第二局各投出两次三振，第三局又添一次，第四局再添两次，这是他本赛季第八次先发至少投出七次三振。
但当牛棚门打开后，打者们继续挥棒落空。右投手Alex Amalfi在两局中投出五次三振。Gage Stanifer（蓝鸟第10号新秀）用三振解决了他所有六个出局数，随后Yondrei Rojas也贡献了两次三振。总的来说，费舍猫队投手群合计送出20次三振，创下队史纪录。
Perry 最多投了75球，多伦多方面在他从汤米·约翰手术复出的首个赛季中继续密切关注他的工作量。他的投球局数今年已经达到职业生涯最高的73又2/3局，并且曾因头部被平飞球击中而缺阵过一段时间。但健康时，他在三个级别中展现出了与MLB Pipeline将他排在第95位相符的实力——自责分率2.81，对手打击率.196，每九局三振12.6次。
Stanifer 本赛季首次以后援身份出场是在8月6日，此后他已七次作为多局后援投手上场。在这段时间里，他在14局中投出22次三振，并将对手打击率限制在.184。凭借他的速球/滑球组合，这被认为是蓝鸟系统中最犀利的组合拳之一，Stanifer在新角色中展现出了持续让打者挥空的能力。
将“椰子鸡柳”加入替补身份家族，是为了给花岗岩州带来一丝甜蜜的夏日气息。但这也为费舍猫队创造历史增添了一点别样的风味。

items.titleEn: With franchise legends in crowd, Blue Jays deliver gritty comeback win
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Sometimes you hit three home runs and cruise to victory, other times you have to grind to give yourself a chance.
On Friday it was the former for the Blue Jays, and Saturday, it was the latter.
Toronto rallied from a three-run deficit to defeat the Mariners, 4-3, in the second game of a three-game series at Rogers Centre.
Seattle jumped out to a 3-0 lead after four innings before walks and a defensive miscue let the Blue Jays back into the game in the bottom of the fifth.
With one out, Mariners starter Kade Anderson allowed a single off the bat of Myles Straw and issued a free pass to Brett Bateman.

Reliever Eduard Bazardo then came on to strike out Alejandro Kirk, but followed it with walks of Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and George Springer. What should’ve resulted in one run on the walk to Springer turned into two when ball four skipped away from catcher Cal Raleigh, allowing Bateman to scamper home from second.
The Blue Jays would score two more in the bottom of the sixth on singles from Bateman and Kirk to take a lead they would never relinquish.
Bateman admitted the play at the plate was closer than he anticipated, but he wanted to try to make something happen given the situation.

“I was rounding third and I looked up and Raleigh didn’t have the ball yet,” Bateman said postgame. “There’s two outs, just trying to be aggressive. It worked out. Live and die by being aggressive on the base paths. As soon as I touched third, my head was looking at home.”

Since his arrival in the big leagues on Aug. 7, Bateman has been the spark plug atop the lineup the Blue Jays have needed. After going 1-for-3 with an RBI and a walk on Saturday, he’s now hitting .329 across 76 at bats.
On the mound, José Soriano recovered from a tough start to the game to throw seven innings. He surrendered three runs on five hits with two walks and six strikeouts.
The entire day got off to an emotional start as the Blue Jays honoured long-time player, manager and broadcaster Buck Martinez by enshrining him in the franchise’s new Hall of Excellence.
It created an atmosphere that players took notice of.

“It was great,” Bateman said about the energy in the stadium. “The ceremony was awesome. I’ve been here a month and I almost teared up. It just shows how strong the community and bond is. I want the building to be like that all the time, and they’ve done that. They give us that energy. It was a great team win.”
Manager John Schneider continues to be impressed with his young leadoff hitter and how comfortable he is with such little experience at the major league level.

“You don’t see that very often,” Schneider said of Bateman scoring from second. “He doesn’t take anything for granted. It’s what we’ve tried to grasp onto a little bit after the Trade Deadline with guys like him and trying to force the issue. I think that kind of re-energized everyone.”
With the Guardians losing on Saturday afternoon, the Blue Jays now sit 1.5 games back of the final American League Wild Card spot.
Schneider was happy with the way his team won two very different games from Friday to Saturday, but ultimately all that matters is coming away with a victory this time of year, he said.

“Every win is going to be important and every win can come in any way, shape or form,” Schneider said. “It starts on the mound, Soriano was really good. Every game is going to be different and good teams find ways to do it in different ways.”
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟在队史传奇面前逆转水手
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟主场4-3逆转水手，Bateman关键跑垒立功，Soriano七局好投，距美联外卡席位仅1.5场。
bodyZh: 多伦多——有时候你打出三支本垒打轻松获胜，有时候你必须努力拼搏才能为自己争取到机会。
周五蓝鸟属于前者，而周六则属于后者。
在罗杰斯中心进行的三场系列赛第二战中，多伦多蓝鸟在落后3分的情况下奋起反击，以4-3击败西雅图水手。
西雅图水手在四局过后取得3-0领先，随后保送和防守失误让蓝鸟在第五局下半局回到比赛中。
一人出局情况下，水手先发投手Kade Anderson被Myles Straw击出安打，随后又保送了Brett Bateman。
后援投手Eduard Bazardo随后登场三振了Alejandro Kirk，但随即又保送了Vladimir Guerrero Jr.和George Springer。本该因保送Springer而只丢一分的局面，却因第四坏球从捕手Cal Raleigh身边弹开而变成丢两分，让Bateman从二垒跑回本垒。
蓝鸟在第六局下半局凭借Bateman和Kirk的安打再得两分，取得领先并此后再未让出。
Bateman承认本垒上的拼抢比他预想的更接近，但在那种情况下他想尝试创造机会。
“我绕过三垒时抬头看，Raleigh还没有接到球，”Bateman赛后说。“当时已经两出局，我只是想积极跑垒。结果奏效了。在垒道上积极跑垒，要么成功要么出局。我一踩上三垒，眼睛就盯住了本垒。”
自8月7日升上大联盟以来，Bateman一直是蓝鸟打线顶端的火花。周六他3打数1安打，贡献1分打点和1次保送，目前76打数打击率为.329。
投手方面，José Soriano在开局艰难的情况下恢复状态，投了七局。他失3分，被击出5支安打，有2次保送和6次三振。
蓝鸟将长期担任球员、主教练和转播员的Buck Martinez请入球队新设立的卓越殿堂，让这一天以激动的气氛开场。
这营造出了一种球员们都能感受到的氛围。
“氛围棒极了，”Bateman谈到球场内的能量时说。“仪式非常精彩。我到这里才一个月，差点就流泪了。这正说明了球队的社区和纽带有多么牢固。我希望这座球馆一直都有这样的气氛，他们也做到了。他们给了我们那样的能量。这是一场伟大的团队胜利。”
主教练John Schneider继续对他年轻的第一棒打者印象深刻，也被他在如此少的大联盟经验下还能如此从容所打动。
“这并不多见，”Schneider谈到Bateman从二垒跑回本垒得分时说。“他从不把任何事视为理所当然。这正是我们在交易截止日之后试图抓住的东西，让像他这样的球员去主动制造机会。我认为这让每个人都重新焕发了活力。”
随着守护者在周六下午输球，蓝鸟现在距离美国联盟外卡最后一个席位还差1.5个胜场。
Schneider对球队从周五到周六以两种截然不同的方式赢球感到高兴，但他表示，在赛季的这个阶段，唯一重要的是带走胜利。
“每一场胜利都至关重要，任何形式的胜利都不例外，”Schneider说。“一切从投手开始，Soriano表现得非常好。每场比赛都会有所不同，优秀的球队会用不同的方式找到取胜之道。”

items.titleEn: Blue Jays legend Buck Martinez inducted into Hall of Excellence
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Forty-five years ago, Buck Martinez got home from a run to find his wife, Arlene, with a bottle of champagne waiting. He’d just been traded from the Brewers to the Blue Jays, and all he could think of was, ‘That’s the best they could do?’

Saturday afternoon, Martinez walked onto the field at Rogers Centre to the loudest ovation this stadium has heard since the World Series. It’s his induction day to the Blue Jays’ Hall of Excellence, where he’s now the 12th member and will forever be enshrined as one of the most beloved figures in this organization’s history.

What a man, what a life, what a story. Martinez still remembers every detail of those early days. There was a deal to the Yankees that fell through, then he rode around with the Brewers as a fourth-string catcher until the Blue Jays came calling, looking for a veteran catcher to help the pitching staff and work with a young Ernie Whitt behind the plate. So much more was waiting for him, though. So many times over the years, he’s called that trade “the best thing that’s ever happened to me.”

“Baseball isn’t about stats, it’s about memories,” Martinez said, “and we’ve experienced a lot of great memories over the years. The city of Toronto has changed my life. This organization, the Toronto Blue Jays, has changed my life. You, the fans, have changed my life. As I enter the Hall of Excellence today, I do so with a heart overwhelmed with gratitude. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for welcoming me into your family. Thank you for letting me tell the story of Toronto Blue Jays baseball.”

The stadium Saturday was filled with people who love Martinez in different ways, but aren’t they all the same? There were former teammates like the great Dave Stieb, then Blue Jays legends who played under Martinez as manager, like Carlos Delgado. Younger fans will know him as the voice of the Blue Jays, that unmistakable voice in your living room, night after night.

“Get up, ball! Get out of here!” Joe Carter shouted, doing his best impression of Martinez Saturday morning. “It’s the enthusiasm he has for the game, then the way he played the game and managed the game. Just being involved in baseball for all of the years he was involved in it, this is a great honor.”

Regardless of which image comes to mind when you first think of Martinez, though, it all comes back to the same place. He connects with people. Whether he’s catching, managing or broadcasting, something about Martinez connects with the player or fan on the other side, making them feel like they’re part of something.

“He’s been here for such a long time and meant so much to so many people,” said Jose Bautista. “Being the voice in so many households, that goes a long way and that stays with people. I’m very happy for him and I’m happy he’s going to be in the Hall with us.”

At the unveiling of the Blue Jays’ new Hall of Excellence Saturday morning, all of these baseball legends lit up when they were asked about Buck. Just like us, all of them have known Martinez at different stages of his legendary career. When he was traded to the Blue Jays, Martinez thought he was “at the end of the line”, but he played six more seasons up to 1986, playing alongside some of this organization’s greats.

“He was an awesome teammate and an awesome person,” Stieb said. “He had a knack to calm me down when things kind of got out of control for me. He just has this way to soothe you and get your focus back into the game, and forget whatever I was mad about.”

Then came his move to broadcasting. Martinez’s full name is John Albert Martinez, and Paul Beeston, always the eccentric, calls him “Albert”. When Martinez’s playing days finally came to an end, Beeston, sitting in that meeting, had an idea.
“Albert…” he said, “do you want to do TV?”

Martinez didn’t have any interest in it. He’d always been a player and that’s all he knew, so he politely declined. By the time he got home and told his wife about this, Arlene made sure that Buck picked that phone right back up and called Beeston. The rest is history, and as Buck likes to say, she was right again.
“He’s been a leader in spreading the gospel of baseball across the country,” Beeston said.

This moment is so rare because Martinez is so rare. Players of past and present, coaches, executives and media members are rarely unanimous on any topic, but Martinez transcends all of those labels he’s worn. He is, to everyone, just “Buck”. He’s the man who feels like your old friend, but just happens to be one of the most important figures in this country’s sports history.
“The only thing I would say to Buck is thank you,” said Vladimir Guerrero Jr., “and I love you, man.”
As Martinez spoke Saturday, players watched on and cheered, friends and colleagues wiped away tears. One last time, we got to hear it.
“Swing and a drive!” Martinez said. “Get up! Get out of here! I’m gone!”
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟传奇 Buck Martinez 入选卓越名人堂
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟传奇 Buck Martinez 入选卓越名人堂，成为第12位成员。
bodyZh: 多伦多 -- 四十五年前，Buck Martinez 跑步回到家中，发现妻子 Arlene 拿着一瓶香槟在等他。他刚刚被从酿酒人交易到蓝鸟，他脑海中只有一个念头：‘他们能做的就这些？’
周六下午，Martinez 走进 Rogers Centre 的球场，收获了这座球场自世界大赛以来最热烈的掌声。这是他入选蓝鸟卓越名人堂的日子，他成为该名人堂的第12位成员，并将作为球队历史上最受爱戴的人物之一被永远铭记。
多么了不起的人，多么了不起的人生，多么了不起的故事。Martinez 仍记得那些早期日子的每一个细节。曾有一笔到洋基队的交易告吹，之后他作为酿酒人的第四替补捕手随队征战，直到蓝鸟找上门来，希望找一位老将捕手帮助投手阵容，并与年轻的 Ernie Whitt 一起在接手区工作。然而，等待他的远不止这些。多年来，他多次称那笔交易是‘发生在我身上最棒的事’。
“棒球不是关于数据，而是关于回忆，”Martinez 说，“这些年来我们经历了许多美好的回忆。多伦多这座城市改变了我的生活。这个组织，多伦多蓝鸟，改变了我的生活。你们，球迷们，改变了我的生活。今天当我进入卓越名人堂时，我带着一颗充满感激的心。感谢你们相信我。感谢你们欢迎我加入你们的家庭。感谢你们让我讲述多伦多蓝鸟棒球的故事。”
周六的球场里坐满了以不同方式爱着 Martinez 的人们，但这些爱难道不是殊途同归吗？有像伟大的 Dave Stieb 这样的前队友，还有曾在 Martinez 担任主教练时效力过的蓝鸟传奇人物，如 Carlos Delgado。年轻的球迷会知道他是蓝鸟的声音，那个每晚在客厅里回荡的独特嗓音。
“起来，球！飞出去！”周六早上，Joe Carter 尽力模仿着 Martinez 喊道。“这是他对比赛的热情，还有他打球和执教的方式。在棒球领域参与这么多年，这是一项伟大的荣誉。”
然而，无论你最初想到 Martinez 时脑海中浮现的是哪种形象，最终都会指向同一个核心。他能与人们建立联系。无论是担任捕手、教练还是解说员，Martinez 身上总有某种特质能连接起对方球员或球迷，让他们感觉自己是一个集体的一部分。
“他在这里待了这么久，对这么多人而言意义重大，”Jose Bautista 说。“成为如此多家庭中的声音，这会产生深远的影响，并留在人们心中。我为他感到非常高兴，也为他将与我们一同进入名人堂感到高兴。”
周六早上，在蓝鸟队新卓越名人堂的揭幕仪式上，当被问及 Buck 时，这些棒球传奇人物都喜形于色。和我们一样，他们都在 Martinez 传奇生涯的不同阶段认识他。当他被交易到蓝鸟时，Martinez 以为自己‘走到了职业生涯的尽头’，但他又打了六个赛季，直到 1986 年，与这支球队的许多伟大球员并肩作战。
“他是个了不起的队友，也是个了不起的人，”Stieb 说。“当我有些失控时，他总有办法让我平静下来。他就是有那种方式安抚你，让你把注意力重新集中到比赛中，忘掉我生气的那些事。”
然后他转向了解说工作。Martinez 的全名是 John Albert Martinez，而 Paul Beeston 一向古怪，总是叫他‘Albert’。当 Martinez 的球员生涯终于结束时，坐在会议中的 Beeston 有了一个主意。
“Albert……”他说，“你想做电视解说吗？”
Martinez 对此并不感兴趣。他一直是球员，他只知道这个，所以他礼貌地拒绝了。当他回到家把这件事告诉妻子时，Arlene 让他立刻拿起电话回电给 Beeston。剩下的就是历史了，正如 Buck 喜欢说的，她又一次是对的。
“他一直是向全国传播棒球福音的领军人物，”Beeston 说。
这一刻如此难得，正因为 Martinez 如此难得。过去的和现在的球员、教练、高管和媒体人很少在任何话题上达成一致，但 Martinez 超越了他所佩戴的所有标签。对每个人来说，他就是‘Buck’。他感觉像是你的老友，但恰好是这个国家体育史上最重要的人物之一。
“我只想对 Buck 说谢谢，”Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 说，“还有，我爱你，伙计。”
周六，当 Martinez 讲话时，球员们在一旁观看并欢呼，朋友和同事们擦去泪水。最后一次，我们得以听到它。
“挥棒，击飞！”Martinez 说。“起来！飞出去！我走了！”

items.titleEn: Blue Jays honor icons with Hall of Excellence
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The gold curtain pulled back to reveal the eight living members of the Blue Jays’ new Hall of Excellence, each of them a franchise icon.

From left to right stood George Bell, Dave Stieb, Joe Carter, Cito Gaston, Carlos Delgado, Jose Bautista, Paul Beeston and Pat Gillick. In the Hall behind them, lockers stood for the late Roy Halladay, Tony Fernandez and Tom Cheek. These 11 men have shaped the Toronto Blue Jays into the organization we know today, and Saturday afternoon in Toronto, they’ll be joined by the great Buck Martinez.

Located on the 100 Level of Rogers Centre, tucked in the right-field corner, the Hall of Excellence is now open to fans, the next step in the Blue Jays’ encouraging efforts to preserve their history and tell those stories while moving this organization forward.
This is what some of the Hall’s members and Blue Jays representatives had to say:
Joe Carter (1991-97):

“What we have left are our memories. It’s great to come back here, talk about baseball and see everybody. When we had the statue unveiling [in July], we lost our great closer, Duane Ward. Our time is very limited. You take advantage of that when you can see these guys like City Gaston and Pat Gillick, then Buck Martinez going into the Hall of Excellence. This is something you don’t take for granted. Tomorrow is never promised for us. To see these guys and be associated with these guys … it’s a great way to cap a lifetime of baseball.”

“This is awesome. Everybody here had such great talent. You’ve got to go out there, give it all and succeed to be here. This is an honor. It’s great that they’ve recognized that and we get our little day in the sun again.”
Jose Bautista (2008-17):

“It’s good to have reminders, right? The little Easter eggs here and there to remind you of the history and what’s happened here with the brand that’s been built over decades. Then, what it means to play Blue Jays baseball. That takes shape over time with the personalities, the style of play and the historical moments. I’m glad to be a part of this and add my little grain of sand to that. This is going to continue to happen. We’re seeing it live with the guys playing today, like Vladdy and others. I’m very happy for the organization, very happy for the fans.”
Carlos Delgado (1993-04):

“This is fantastic. It is so important to remember the history of our franchise. They talk about us as a ‘new’ franchise, but it’s 50 years. There are a lot of great players who have played on this field and [Exhibition Stadium]. Having an opportunity to show people where the Blue Jays come from, it gives the city and the fans an opportunity to identify with the franchise. They did a great job. This is a beautiful space.”
President and CEO Mark Shapiro:

“Thirty years ago, the Blue Jays established the Level of Excellence to recognize individuals whose contributions helped define this organization. Today, we are building on that legacy. The Hall of Excellence creates a permanent home for the stories, achievement and memories of the players and leaders who helped build this franchise and shape Blue Jays history … The individuals represented here established the foundation of this organization and we are proud to ensure that their stories will continue to be told for years to come.”
Manager John Schneider:

“It’s a really cool way to remind people of the history of the organization. It’s cool to see names and numbers up on the stadium, but you can’t really feel them or touch them. Being physically closer to it, the example you go to is obviously Monument Park at Yankee Stadium. It’s here, it’s displayed for people to see and to learn more about the [players]. I think this is great, and the statue of Joe Carter is great. Whenever fans or players can get closer to that, I think it’s really good.”

The Hall is rich with memorabilia, too, including stunning display cases for the club’s Gold Glove and Silver Slugger winners. Some of the artifacts are obvious, like bats and gloves, but then there are some gems, like Delgado’s notebook where he took intricate notes on pitchers, or the cigar boxes in Beeston’s display, perfectly capturing the one-of-a-kind character.
This space will now be open to fans at all times, and as the Blue Jays continue to expand this Hall and what it holds, fans will have a voice in voting for who is inducted next.
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟设立卓越殿堂致敬传奇
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟队正式启用卓越殿堂，致敬队史传奇。
bodyZh: 多伦多——金色帷幕拉开，露出蓝鸟队新卓越殿堂的八位在世成员，他们都是球队标志性人物。

从左到右依次是George Bell、Dave Stieb、Joe Carter、Cito Gaston、Carlos Delgado、Jose Bautista、Paul Beeston和Pat Gillick。在他们身后的大厅里，储物柜代表着已故的Roy Halladay、Tony Fernandez和Tom Cheek。这11位将多伦多蓝鸟塑造成了我们今天所知的球队，周六下午在多伦多，伟大的Buck Martinez也将加入他们。
卓越殿堂位于罗杰斯中心100层看台，右外野角落，现已向球迷开放，这是蓝鸟队在推动球队前进的同时，保护历史并讲述这些故事的鼓舞人心的努力中的下一步。
以下是部分殿堂成员和蓝鸟队代表的话：
Joe Carter（1991-97年）：

“我们所剩下的就是回忆。回到这里，谈论棒球，见到大家，真是太好了。当我们在（7月）雕像揭幕时，我们失去了伟大的终结者Duane Ward。我们的时间非常有限。当你能看到像Cito Gaston和Pat Gillick这些人，然后Buck Martinez进入卓越殿堂时，你必须珍惜。这是我们不能想当然的事情。明天对我们来说从未有保证。看到这些人，并与他们联系在一起……这是为棒球生涯画上句号的好方式。”
Dave Stieb（1979-92年、‘98年）：
“这太棒了。这里的每个人都才华横溢。你必须走出去，全力以赴并取得成功才能站在这里。这是一种荣誉。他们认可了这一点，我们又能再次迎来属于我们的高光时刻，这太棒了。”
Jose Bautista（2008-17年）：
“有这些提醒是好事，对吧？这里那里的小彩蛋让你想起历史，想起几十年来建立起的品牌所发生的事情。然后是效力蓝鸟队意味着什么。这随着时间推移，通过个性、打法和历史时刻逐渐形成。我很高兴成为其中一员，为之添砖加瓦。这将继续发生。我们正通过今天打球的球员，如Vladdy等人，亲眼目睹这一切。我为球队感到非常高兴，为球迷感到非常高兴。”
Carlos Delgado（1993-04年）：
“这太棒了。记住我们球队的历史非常重要。他们把我们当作一支‘新’球队，但已经有50年了。在这片球场和Exhibition Stadium上打过球的伟大球员有很多。有机会向人们展示蓝鸟队的来历，让这座城市和球迷有机会认同这支球队。他们做得很好。这是一个美丽的地方。”
总裁兼首席执行官Mark Shapiro：
“三十年前，蓝鸟队设立了卓越荣誉榜来表彰那些贡献卓著、帮助定义这支球队的个人。今天，我们在此基础上继续发展。卓越殿堂为那些帮助建立球队、塑造蓝鸟历史的球员和领袖的故事、成就和回忆提供了一个永久的家园……这里所代表的个人奠定了这支球队的基础，我们自豪地确保他们的故事将在未来多年继续流传。”
主教练John Schneider：
“这是一种让人们铭记球队历史的好方式。看到体育场上的名字和号码很棒，但你无法真正感受到它们或触摸它们。通过物理上更接近它，你想到的例子显然是洋基体育场的纪念碑公园。它就在这里，被展示给人们看，让他们了解更多关于（球员）的信息。我认为这很棒，Joe Carter的雕像也很棒。无论何时，只要球迷或球员能更加接近这些，我认为都非常好。”
这座殿堂还拥有丰富的纪念品，包括为俱乐部金手套奖和银棒奖得主设立的惊艳展示柜。一些物品一目了然，比如球棒和手套，但还有一些珍品，比如Delgado记录投手详细笔记的笔记本，或者Beeston展柜中的雪茄盒，完美展现了其独一无二的个性。
这个空间现在将随时向球迷开放，随着蓝鸟队不断扩大这座殿堂及其内容，球迷将有机会参与投票，决定下一位入选者。

items.titleEn: Cease pads Cy case with yet another gem to right Blue Jays' ship
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The easiest way to forget an ugly loss that brought boos down from the home crowd? Hand the ball to Dylan Cease.

The ace was spectacular yet again, leading the Blue Jays to an 8-1 win over the Mariners to open their weekend series at Rogers Centre. With that, the Blue Jays are now 2 1/2 games back of the Guardians for the final Wild Card spot.
This is what mattered most:
1. Cy Young battle down to the home stretch
You could have predicted Cease’s line an hour before first pitch. Six innings, one earned run, eight strikeouts and another dominant performance.

The AL Cy Young race is down to Cease and Cam Schlittler of the Yankees, who countered with 5 2/3 scoreless innings (5 BB, 8 K) against the Red Sox Friday night. This could turn into a fascinating debate by the end of September, highlighting which statistics are valued most.

Manager John Schneider points to WHIP and quality starts as two of the more common metrics that he gives some added weight to. If he were running Cease’s Cy Young campaign, he’d highlight the reliability of Cease’s outings -- not just the dominance of his stuff -- and how rare this level of consistency is in the modern game.

“Just because of the way bullpens are used,” Schneider said. “When he’s out there, we’re pretty comfortable with him getting deep into the game. That impacts what you do in the days before and the days after.”
Cease has also struck out seven or more batters in 19 consecutive starts. The last pitcher to do that in a single season was Randy Johnson in 2001.
2. Add-on homers? The Blue Jays?
This is what it’s supposed to look like.

Both Nathan Lukes and George Springer tacked on solo shots to give the Blue Jays some extra cushion after they took a 3-1 lead in the first. These were both trademark swings, too, with Lukes dropping down to a knee to launch one out while Springer nearly toppled over, that all-effort swing connecting on a towering blast to left.

Watching that ball fly out, it immediately brought back the memory of Springer’s home run against the Mariners in Game 7 of the ALCS, which ultimately sent them to the World Series. We’re still too close to the heartbreak of 2025 for that moment to be fully appreciated and contextualized, but it will forever stand as one of the biggest moments in this organization’s history.

After that pair of homers in the fifth, Kazuma Okamoto joined the party with his 27th of the season an inning later. If the Blue Jays are going to pull off another run in September, power needs to be part of it. That’s a non-negotiable at this point, and it’s the Blue Jays’ only pathway to a winning streak longer than four games, which is their season high.
3. Vlad Watch: 11 home games remain

The box score will show an RBI double for Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and a flyout in his next at-bat. Oddly enough, that flyout was probably a more impressive swing, a line drive straight at the right fielder, while the double was a chopper up the third-base line with some good fortune behind it.

Either way, Guerrero has 11 home games left in the Blue Jays’ final 26, and he still hasn’t homered at Rogers Centre. Around the clubhouse and on the field pregame, Guerrero was loose and energetic, but of course he’s aware of this. After Friday’s win, his OPS sits at just .685.
The Blue Jays only have one shortcut to the final AL Wild Card spot, and it’s Guerrero.
items.titleZh: Cease再献佳作助蓝鸟回正轨，巩固赛扬奖争夺
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟8-1胜水手，Cease六局失一分并送出8次三振，球队距外卡席位差2.5场。
bodyZh: 多伦多——想要忘记一场让主场球迷嘘声四起的糟糕失利，最简单的方法是什么？把球交给 Dylan Cease。
这位王牌投手再次展现超凡状态，带领蓝鸟在罗杰斯中心以8-1战胜水手，开启周末系列赛。由此，蓝鸟在争夺最后一个外卡席位时，落后守护者2.5个胜场。
以下是本场比赛最重要的话题：
1. 赛扬奖之争进入最后冲刺阶段
在首球投出前一个小时，你就能预测到 Cease 的表现数据：六局，一分自责分，八次三振，又是一场统治级表现。
美联赛扬奖的竞争目前集中在 Cease 和洋基的 Cam Schlittler 身上，后者周五晚对阵红袜投了5.2局无失分（5次保送，8次三振）。到九月底，这可能演变成一场有趣的争论，凸显哪些统计指标最受重视。
主教练 John Schneider 指出，WHIP 和优质先发是他更看重的两项常见指标。如果由他来为 Cease 的赛扬奖造势，他会强调 Cease 出场表现的可靠性——不仅仅是其球威的统治力——以及在现代比赛中这种稳定性有多么罕见。
“正因为牛棚的使用方式，”Schneider 说，“当他在场上时，我们很放心他能投长局数。这会影响到前几天和后几天的安排。”
Cease 已经连续19场先发至少三振七名打者。上一次有投手在单赛季做到这一点是2001年的 Randy Johnson。
2. 追加本垒打？蓝鸟？
这才是该有的样子。
Nathan Lukes 和 George Springer 各自击出阳春炮，为蓝鸟在首局取得3-1领先后增添保险分。这也是两人标志性的挥棒——Lukes 单膝跪地轰出一发，而 Springer 几乎失去平衡，全力挥棒将球轰向左外野的高飞本垒打。
看着那球飞出，立刻让人想起 Springer 在美联冠军赛第七战对阵水手队时的那支本垒打，那记本垒打最终将他们送进了世界大赛。我们离2025年的痛楚还太近，那个时刻还未被完全欣赏和解读，但它将永远载入这支球队历史上最重要的时刻之一。
在第五局那两记本垒打之后，Kazuma Okamoto 一局后也加入派对，轰出他本赛季第27号。如果蓝鸟想在九月再掀起一波连胜，长打火力必须成为其中的一部分。这在现在是不可妥协的要求，也是蓝鸟唯一能实现超过四连胜（本赛季最长连胜）的途径。
3. Vlad 观察：剩余11场主场比赛
技术统计将显示 Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 打出一支打点二垒安打，以及下一次打席的飞球出局。奇怪的是，那次飞球出局可能是更令人印象深刻的挥棒——一记直飞右外野手的平飞球，而那支二垒安打则是一记沿三垒线的内野弹跳球，带有一些运气成分。
无论如何，在蓝鸟最后的26场比赛中，Guerrero 还有11场主场比赛，而他仍然未能在罗杰斯中心击出本垒打。在赛前休息室和场上，Guerrero 看起来轻松而充满活力，但他当然也知道这一点。周五取胜后，他的 OPS 只有 .685。
蓝鸟要拿到最后一个美联外卡席位，只有一条捷径，那就是 Guerrero。

items.titleEn: Taillon makes 1st rehab start, could return to Blue Jays soon
items.summaryEn: Infielder Smith (hamstring) also on comeback trail
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Friday was a busy night for rehabbing big leaguers with the Triple-A Buffalo Bisons, headlined by starter Jameson Taillon.

Working his way back from right forearm tendinitis, Taillon may only need the long rehab appearance before returning to the Blue Jays, who are still trying to elbow their way back into the AL Wild Card race.

Infielder Josh Smith (left hamstring) also played in Friday night’s game, his second in a row with the Bisons. Smith may stick with the Bisons for another day or two to get more at-bats, but he is expected to be back with the Blue Jays on Sept. 1, when rosters expand, at the latest.
How did Taillon perform?

Taillon breezed through the first three innings on less than 30 pitches, but ran into trouble in the fourth inning. He ended with four runs charged over 3 1/3 innings, which included three hits, two walks and two strikeouts.

Taillon’s velocities were slightly below his MLB averages from this season, which can be “normal” in these Triple-A rehab appearances, but the Blue Jays will need to determine how much that final inning matters. Up until then, Taillon worked extremely quickly and filled up the strike zone.
He ended the night with 48 pitches, which should set him up to throw over 60 next time out.
What’s next?

The Blue Jays would like to slide Taillon right back into their rotation the next time through, even if he’s not fully built up. That’s essentially what they’ve done recently with Spencer Arrighetti, who came off the IL and gave the Blue Jays pitch counts of 61 and 79 his first two outings.
There’s room for the Blue Jays to use Monday’s off-day and tinker with their rotation, but at the very least, Taillon is not here to be another bulk option out of the bullpen. He’s expected to start.
What are they saying?
We’ve seen Taillon twice in a Blue Jays uniform, a pair of four-inning appearances. His second was a clear step forward, too, holding the Red Sox scoreless.

Taillon had struggled with the Cubs earlier this season prior to the trade, but the Blue Jays believed that a mental refresh could help the longtime big leaguer get back on track. This is exactly what Taillon highlighted when he met with the media for the first time following that trade, an open and honest critique of his own season to that point.

“I got to a point where I was pitching a little timid,” Taillon said. “That’s not me. I was thinking about the worst-case scenario sometimes. ... 'I want to get ahead, but I don’t want to leak this towards the middle and give up another home run,' so I was out there with those thoughts. That’s just a horrible place to be. That’s the human side, so getting to take a step back and getting a fresh start, I want to get back to who I am, which is filling up the zone with six pitches and being super aggressive.”
What else?
On Thursday, the Blue Jays signed 12-year veteran Michael Lorenzen, who’d recently been released by the Rockies after a difficult season in their rotation (7.08 ERA).

Lorenzen was thrown right into the fire, coming out of the bullpen in the 13-2 blowout loss to the Royals on Thursday, but he’ll be available in any role the Blue Jays need. It still feels like the Blue Jays want to get Taillon back as quickly as possible, but if they need additional time for any reason, Lorenzen is an option along with CJ Van Eyk or Chad Dallas for length.
items.titleZh: Taillon 完成首次复健先发，或很快回归蓝鸟
items.summaryZh: 内野手 Smith（腿筋伤势）也在康复路上。
bodyZh: 多伦多——周五晚对于在3A水牛城野牛队进行康复的大联盟球员来说是忙碌的一晚，其中以先发投手 Jameson Taillon 为主角。
Taillon 正在从右前臂肌腱炎中恢复，他可能只需要这次长时间康复出场就能回归蓝鸟，而蓝鸟仍在努力重返美国联盟外卡竞争行列。
内野手 Josh Smith（左腿筋）也参加了周五晚的比赛，这是他连续第二场随野牛队出战。Smith 可能会在野牛队再待一两天以获得更多打席，但预计他最迟将于9月1日大联盟名单扩编时回归蓝鸟。
Taillon 表现如何？
Taillon 用不到30球轻松投完前三局，但在第四局遇到麻烦。他最终在 3 1/3 局中被击出3支安打，送出2次保送和2次三振，失4分（自责分）。
Taillon 的球速略低于本赛季的大联盟平均水平，这在3A复健赛中可能属“正常现象”，但蓝鸟需要判断最后一局的影响有多大。在那之前，Taillon 投球节奏极快，且不断将球投进好球带。
他当晚共投了48球，这应该能让他下一次出场投球数超过60球。
接下来是什么？
蓝鸟希望在下一次轮值时就将他直接放回先发轮值，即使他还未完全恢复投球量。这基本上就是他们最近对 Spencer Arrighetti 所做的，他从伤病名单回来后，前两次先发分别投了61球和79球。
蓝鸟可以利用周一的休息日调整轮值，但至少 Taillon 并不是作为牛棚里的另一个长局数人选。他预计将先发。
他们怎么说？
我们已经两次看到 Taillon 身穿蓝鸟球衣出场，两次都是投四局。他的第二次表现明显进步，让红袜一分未得。
Taillon 本赛季在被交易前效力于小熊队时表现挣扎，但蓝鸟认为心态上的刷新能帮助这位老将重回正轨。这正是 Taillon 在交易后首次与媒体见面时所强调的，他对彼时自己的赛季进行了公开而诚实的评价。
Taillon 说：“我曾经到了投球时有些胆怯的地步。那不是真正的我。有时我会想到最坏的情况……‘我想抢好球数，但我不想把球投到中路又被打出本垒打’，所以我带着这种想法投球。那真是个糟糕的境地。这就是人性的一面，所以能够退一步重新开始，我想找回真正的自己，即用六种球路塞满好球带，并且极具侵略性。”
还有什么？
周四，蓝鸟签下了拥有12年大联盟经验的老将 Michael Lorenzen，他刚刚被洛矶队裁掉，此前他在洛矶队先发轮值中度过了一个艰难赛季（自责分率7.08）。
Lorenzen 立刻被投入到实战中，在周四13-2惨败给皇家的比赛中从牛棚登板。他可以在蓝鸟需要的任何角色中待命。感觉蓝鸟仍希望尽快让 Taillon 回归，但如果他们因任何原因需要更多时间，Lorenzen 以及 CJ Van Eyk 或 Chad Dallas 都是可提供局数的选项。

items.titleEn: For Blue Jays' historic all-Italian battery, they're ready for the moment
bodyEn: The two ballplayers had never met before arriving in Dunedin, Fla., swapping out Italy’s azzurri blue for the Blue Jays’ shade. But now Giaconino Lasaracina and Giacomo Taschin are together. Not just as teammates and road trip roomies for the Single-A ballclub, though: They just might be the first all-Italian developed battery in affiliated baseball history.

“It’s funny: We never faced each other in Italy,” Lasaracina told MLB.com, with Javier Román translating. “I knew him because he was playing for the Italian U-18s, but we were always in different groups. But when I signed with the Blue Jays, he was one of the first people to send me a text and congratulate me.”
It’s also helped the duo communicate more easily, too: Taschin speaks Italian and English; Lasaracina Spanish and Italian.

“I have a guy I can speak Italian with, even when we’re in the game,” Taschin said. “If I need some advice, we can speak Italian without problems. He’s a great guy and we talk a lot, even outside of baseball.”
Forget covering their mouths with their mitts during mound visits, too. It's like they have a secret language.
“We know that nobody speaks Italian, so I can tell him a couple words in Italian,” Lasaracina joked.

Though they now share a locker room and a language, their paths to the Minors couldn’t have been more different. For both, getting noticed meant relying upon an idea that Italian national team manager and former big leaguer Francisco Cervelli has preached across the country: “You never know who’s watching.”

Standing a muscular 6-foot-3 and 210 pounds, Lasaracina cuts an imposing figure at the dish. He’s shown off that power recently, hitting the longest home run in Dunedin Blue Jays Statcast history with a 457-foot, 112.4 mph blast last week. It was his first of two homers in the game, but the catcher thinks his second was actually the more impressive of the two no matter what the numbers say.

“I felt that I hit it hard, but I didn’t know it was that long,” Lasaracina said. “In fact, I thought my second homer was a little longer because it went higher. But honestly, at that moment, I felt really happy because that was my plan. And the moment you have a plan and can execute it, you feel really good.”

Watching that blast, you’d assume that Lasaracina had scouts drooling over him from the day he first picked up a bat. But growing up in Carupano, Venezuela, Lasaracina was surrounded by plenty of other baseball prodigies. When he realized scouts weren’t interested in him as a teenager, he was left with few options.

“My parents were the ones that kept pushing me forward to keep practicing,” Lasaracina said. “At one point, I was like, ‘I don't want to practice anymore.’ But my parents told me, ‘No, keep ready, be prepared, because you never know who's watching you.”

It was good advice. Thanks to a tip from a friend living in Italy, he sent a video of himself taking swings and playing all over the field -- first, third, behind the plate. Settimo, in Italy’s Serie A, liked what they saw and quickly installed the then-18-year-old in its lineup.
“One of the teams there in Italy took the chance on me,” Lasaracina said. “And thank God for that.”

Despite his youth -- and like Ted Williams all those decades ago -- he hit .406 to pace the team. (One of his teammates that season, Williams Wong, signed with the Rangers as a 17-year-old the next year.)

Lasaracina continued to improve over the years, culminating in a breakout at the 2025 European Baseball Championship. Making his senior national team debut, Lasaracina slashed .481/.516/1.185 with a tournament-leading six home runs. The performance cemented Lasaracina in the national team’s plans and the 22-year-old was preparing to play in this spring’s World Baseball Classic when the Blue Jays came calling.

“Every time I remember [getting the offer from the Blue Jays], I get so happy because it was something totally unexpected,” Lasaracina said. “By then, I was already 22 years old, and usually they look for 16- or 17-year-olds. They almost never sign 18-year-olds, so at 20-plus years old, it's very difficult.”
While Lasaracina took a winding path from Venezuela to Serie A, Taschin's experience was, by European standards at least, much more direct.

He was born in the ancient town of Rovigo, a city of about 50,000 in northeast Italy. Italy may be the land of soccer, but Taschin’s father and older brother were ballplayers, ensuring that Taschin’s future was on the ballfield.
“It started with my Dad and my brother playing baseball,” Taschin said. “I always had a partner, so I could play catch with someone.”

The left-hander caught scout’s attention when he won the MVP at the 2024 U-18 European Baseball Championship. Playing as a two-way player, he hit .333 with one home run and eight RBIs, while posting a remarkable 1.00 ERA and striking out 22 batters in 14 innings. Perhaps more impressive -- especially for a young pitcher -- he walked only three.
All of that led to this spring when Taschin officially signed with the Blue Jays as a 19-year-old. There was just one catch: He was still in high school.

“It was kind of weird because when I signed, I came here to Florida for one week to see the complex and then meet the coaches,” Taschin said. “Then after I signed here and after my medical, I had to come back to Italy to finish high school.”
Forget senior-itis, Taschin had to spend his last three weeks of school preparing to become a professional ballplayer.
“They were surprised, because for us,” Taschin said about his high school friends, "MLB is something new, something [very unexpected] for Italy.”

The hope is that novelty is rapidly changing. There’s Sam Aldegheri, the Angels pitcher who became the first Italian-developed pitcher in MLB history, and has seen big league action in each of the last three seasons. He’s provided a blueprint for Italian ballplayers to follow.

“He played against my brother, so I’m going to say yes: If he made the Majors, I can make the Majors,” Taschin said with a smile. “I can see that Aldegheri is in a good spot, which gives me a chance.”

Though much of the roster consisted of Americans with Italian heritage, the national team’s semifinal run in this spring’s World Baseball Classic reached the sporting newspapers back in Italy and the country’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, mentioned their success in a speech to parliament.

“The very beautiful thing was that this was a united team, and I think that made the difference,” Taschin said. “Italians liked the representation from the guys over there, like the coffee machine and all the celebrations they did. I think the light was turned on after the World Baseball Classic.”

The dream, as espoused by Cervelli and national team captain Vinnie Pasquantino, is that in 20 years, the national team will be filled with players like Lasaracina and Taschin instead of Americans with heritage.

To help build that future, Cervelli now lives and works in Italy for half the year. In addition to the senior Italian team, he manages the U-23 squad, has an academy in Castiglione della Pescaia and helps coach Florence’s Serie A club. He’s referred to himself as a truck driver, motoring up and down the country, to find players like the Blue Jays' duo and help develop them.
He’s seen the impact that the World Baseball Classic has already had on the youth in the nation and he hopes to keep driving it.

“It’s huge. In Italy, a lot of people talk about it,” Cervelli said while the team was at Haarlem Honkbalweek earlier this summer. “I think it's the first time -- and the players felt it -- that they want to represent Italy in the WBC, because that's the biggest tournament, so that's what we're preparing for. I hope I can bring more guys from here to the WBC. They play good baseball, I’ve got an amazing team, and we're growing.”
It helped inspire Taschin, too.

“I think the dream of every player in Italy is to represent the country on the big stage and in international competitions,” Taschin said. “If Team Italy called me, I would say yes every time, because it's my dream. To play for my country, it’s one of the best things that you can do as a baseball player.”
For Lasaracina, the impact is even more immediate. While the catcher credits Cervelli with help on some techniques behind the plate, the much more important lesson was the mental element.
“Francisco told me, ‘Control whatever you can control,’” Lasaracina said. “The external stuff that you can’t control? Just forget about it. Be you and be prepared.”

That’s good advice for any ballplayer, but for players from non-traditional baseball countries, it’s all the more necessary. It may be a more difficult path to forge, but when the opportunity arrives, you need to be ready to take it.

“I’m an old person for the system,” Lasaracina said, “but I never give up. I keep practicing. I tell everyone, keep working hard, keep getting those chances and be able to play in any leagues: Double-A, independent leagues, semiprofessional. You never know who’s going to see you, and you need to be ready for that moment.”
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟历史性全意大利投捕组合蓄势待发
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟队出现史上首对意大利青训体系培养的投捕组合，二人已做好准备。
bodyZh: 这两名球员在抵达佛罗里达州达尼丁之前从未见过面，他们换下意大利的天蓝球衣，穿上蓝鸟队的球衣。但现在，Giaconino Lasaracina和Giacomo Taschin聚在了一起。不仅是作为这支1A球队的队友和客场室友，他们还可能是附属棒球历史上首对完全由意大利培养的投捕组合。
“这很有趣：我们在意大利从未交过手，”Lasaracina通过Javier Román的翻译告诉MLB.com，“我认识他是因为他效力于意大利U-18队，但我们总是分在不同组。不过当我与蓝鸟签约时，他是最早给我发短信祝贺我的人之一。”
这也让两人的沟通变得更加容易：Taschin会说意大利语和英语；Lasaracina会说西班牙语和意大利语。
“我有一个可以用意大利语交流的伙伴，即使在比赛中也是如此，”Taschin说，“如果我需要建议，我们可以毫无问题地用意大利语交流。他是个很棒的人，我们聊很多，甚至不限于棒球。”
投手丘会面时也不用再用手套遮住嘴巴了。就像他们有一种秘密语言。
“我们知道没人会说意大利语，所以我可以用意大利语跟他说几个词，”Lasaracina开玩笑说。
尽管他们现在共享一个更衣室和一种语言，但他们通往小联盟的路径却截然不同。对两人而言，被注意到都依赖于意大利国家队主教练、前大联盟球员Francisco Cervelli在全国宣扬的一个理念：“你永远不知道谁在看你。”
Lasaracina体格强壮，身高6英尺3英寸，体重210磅，在打击区是位令人望而生畏的人物。他最近展示了自己的力量，上周打出457英尺、出口速度112.4英里/小时的轰天炮，是蓝鸟达尼丁队Statcast历史上最远的本垒打。那是他该场两支本垒打中的第一支，但这位捕手认为，无论数据怎么说，他的第二支实际上更令人印象深刻。
“我感觉我打得很重，但我不知道它那么远，”Lasaracina说，“事实上，我认为我的第二支本垒打更远一些，因为它飞得更高。但老实说，那一刻我感觉非常开心，因为那是我的计划。当你制定计划并能够执行时，你会感觉非常好。”
看到那记重炮，你会以为Lasaracina从第一次拿起球棒起就让球探垂涎欲滴。但他在委内瑞拉卡鲁帕诺长大，身边有许多其他棒球神童。当他意识到自己少年时球探对他不感兴趣时，他几乎没有什么选择。
“是我的父母一直推动我继续练习，”Lasaracina说，“曾经有一度，我说：‘我不想再练了。’但我父母告诉我：‘不，保持状态，做好准备，因为你不知道谁在看你。’”
那是好建议。多亏一位住在意大利的朋友的建议，他寄出了一段自己在场上四处挥棒和守备的视频——一垒、三垒、本垒板后面。意大利Serie A的Settimo队看中了他们所见，迅速将当时18岁的他放进先发阵容。
“意大利那里的一支球队给了我机会，”Lasaracina说，“谢天谢地。”
尽管年轻，而且如同几十年前的Ted Williams那样，他击出.406的打击率领先全队。（当季他的一名队友Williams Wong第二年以17岁之龄与游骑兵签约。）
Lasaracina多年来不断进步，最终在2025年欧洲棒球锦标赛上迎来爆发。首次代表国家队出场，Lasaracina交出.481/.516/1.185的打击三围，并以六支本垒打领跑赛事。这一表现巩固了他在国家队的地位，这位22岁球员正准备参加今年春天的世界棒球经典赛，此时蓝鸟找上门来。
“每次想起（收到蓝鸟报价），我就非常开心，因为那是完全出乎意料的，”Lasaracina说，“那时我已经22岁了，通常他们会找16、17岁的球员。他们几乎从不签18岁的，所以20多岁更难。”
Lasaracina从委内瑞拉到意大利Serie A的路径曲折，而Taschin的经历，至少按欧洲标准，要直接得多。
他出生在意大利东北部约5万人口的古城罗维戈。意大利可能是足球的国度，但Taschin的父亲和哥哥都是棒球手，确保了Taschin的未来在球场上。
“一切始于我爸爸和哥哥打棒球，”Taschin说，“我总是有一个伙伴，可以和我一起传接球。”
这位左投手在2024年U-18欧洲棒球锦标赛上获得MVP，吸引了球探注意。作为二刀流球员，他打击率.333，一支本垒打，八分打点，同时防御率仅为1.00，14局中三振22名打者。也许更令人印象深刻的是——尤其是对一位年轻投手而言——他只保送三人。
这一切促成了今年春天，Taschin以19岁之龄正式与蓝鸟签约。只有一个障碍：他还在上高中。
“这有点奇怪，因为我签约时，来佛罗里达待了一周看基地，然后见了教练，”Taschin说，“然后我在这里签约，完成体检后，我必须回意大利完成高中学业。”
别说什么高三倦怠，Taschin必须在他最后三周上学期间为成为职业球员做准备。
“他们很惊讶，因为对我们来说，”Taschin谈到他的高中朋友时说，“MLB是新鲜事物，对意大利来说是非常意想不到的。”
希望这种新鲜感正在迅速改变。有天使队投手Sam Aldegheri，他是MLB历史上首位意大利培养的投手，过去三个赛季都曾在大联盟亮相。他为意大利球员提供了可遵循的蓝图。
“他和我哥哥交过手，所以我要说是的：如果他进了大联盟，我也能进大联盟，”Taschin笑着说，“我可以看到Aldegheri处于不错的位置，这给了我机会。”
尽管名单上许多球员是有意大利血统的美国人，但国家队在今年春天世界棒球经典赛上闯入四强，登上了意大利体育报纸，该国总理Giorgia Meloni在议会演讲中也提到了他们的成功。
“最美妙的是这是一支团结的球队，我认为那是关键，”Taschin说，“意大利人喜欢他们的代表方式，比如咖啡机和所有的庆祝。我认为世界棒球经典赛之后，灯被点亮了。”
Cervelli和队长Vinnie Pasquantino所倡导的梦想是，20年后，国家队将充满像Lasaracina和Taschin这样的球员，而不是有意大利血统的美国人。
为了帮助建设这一未来，Cervelli现在每年有半年生活在意大利工作。除了意大利国家队，他管理U-23队，在佩斯卡亚堡有一所学院，并帮助执教佛罗伦萨的Serie A俱乐部。他称自己为卡车司机，在全国来回奔波，寻找像蓝鸟这对组合那样的球员并帮助培养他们。
他看到了世界棒球经典赛已经对这个国家的年轻人产生的影响，他希望继续推动。
“这意义重大。在意大利，很多人谈论这件事，”Cervelli在今年夏天早些时候球队参加哈勒姆棒球周时说道，“我认为这是第一次——球员们也感受到了——他们想代表意大利参加WBC，因为那是最大的赛事，所以那是我们正在准备的。我希望我能从这儿带更多人参加WBC。他们打出很棒的棒球，我有一支出色的球队，我们正在成长。”
这也激励了Taschin。
“我认为每个意大利球员的梦想都是代表国家登上大舞台，参加国际比赛，”Taschin说，“如果意大利国家队叫我，我每次都会说是，因为那是我的梦想。为国家打球，是棒球运动员能做的最好的事情之一。”
对Lasaracina而言，影响更为直接。尽管这位捕手感谢Cervelli在本垒板后的一些技术上给予帮助，但更重要的教训是心理层面。
“Francisco告诉我：‘控制你能控制的，’”Lasaracina说，“那些你无法控制的外部事物？忘掉它。做自己，做好准备。”
这对任何球员都是好建议，但对来自非传统棒球国家的球员来说，更是必不可少的。这可能需要开辟一条更艰难的道路，但当机会到来时，你需要准备好抓住它。
“按体系标准，我已经是老人了，”Lasaracina说，“但我从不放弃。我持续练习。我告诉每个人，继续努力，抓住机会，能够打任何级别的联赛：2A、独立联盟、半职业。你永远不知道谁会看到你，你需要为那一刻做好准备。”

items.titleEn: Blue Jays add Lorenzen -- and he's ready to 'throw 100 pitches today'
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The Blue Jays signed veteran right-hander Michael Lorenzen, who is active for Thursday’s game against the Royals to provide bullpen depth.

Lorenzen was recently released by the Rockies after posting a 7.08 ERA over 115 2/3 innings, but the Blue Jays are hoping to capture more of what Lorenzen accomplished earlier in his 12-year MLB career. He knows the Royals well, too, after pitching for them in 2024-25, and that level of institutional knowledge has some value.
At this point of the season, any player available in free agency is likely there for a reason, but the Blue Jays see a pathway for Lorenzen supplying some value.

“His availability for length and availability to do a lot of things with our bullpen being in flux [are helpful],” Blue Jays manager John Schneider said. “You pick up a guy who’s done it before and who can basically throw every day. I was just talking to him and he said he can throw every day. He’s here and ready to help.”

It can be energizing to find another opportunity, too. Lorenzen’s numbers with the Rockies weren’t pretty, and this late in the season, that wasn’t going to get him a job with a legitimate World Series contender. Landing with the Blue Jays, though, at least gives him an outside shot at contributing to a postseason run. Lorenzen has been around this league as both a starter and reliever, so he’s seen a lot, but has made just six postseason appearances.
When he showed up to Rogers Centre on Thursday, Lorenzen sat down with Schneider and made it very clear that he’d do anything to help the team.
“[Lorenzen] said, ‘Literally, whatever you want. I could throw 100 pitches today if you need me to. You can try to break me. It’s not going to work,’” Schneider said.

This means a bullpen role in the short term, but if Lorenzen can stick around, his future role could be tied to Jameson Taillon. The Blue Jays just pulled off a successful bullpen day on Wednesday against the Royals, but after Taillon makes a rehab start with Triple-A Buffalo on Friday, they’re open to him sliding back into the rotation the next time through.

That’s still Plan A, but if Taillon needs another rehab start or anything else goes wrong in this rotation -- which has become common -- then Lorenzen gives the Blue Jays another layer of starting depth.
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟签下洛伦岑，他已准备好“今天投100球”
bodyZh: 多伦多——蓝鸟队签下了老将右投手 Michael Lorenzen，他将出战周四对阵皇家队的比赛，以提供牛棚深度。
洛伦岑最近被洛矶队裁掉，本赛季他出战115又2/3局，自责分率为7.08，但蓝鸟队希望他能重现12年大联盟生涯早期的一些表现。他也很了解皇家队，因为他在2024-25赛季曾为他们效力，这种熟悉度具有一定价值。
在赛季的这个阶段，任何在自由球员市场上可用的球员很可能都有其被释放的原因，但蓝鸟队看到了洛伦岑能提供价值的途径。
“他能够投长局数，并且在牛棚不稳定时能做好多事情，”蓝鸟队主教练 John Schneider 说。“你签下一个有过经验、基本上每天都能投球的人。我刚刚和他谈过，他说他每天都可以投。他在这里，随时准备提供帮助。”
找到另一个机会也可能令人振奋。洛伦岑在洛矶队的数字并不好看，而在赛季如此深入时，这不会让他在一支真正有竞争力的世界大赛球队获得工作。不过，加入蓝鸟队至少给了他一个在季后赛征程中做出贡献的机会。洛伦岑在大联盟既当过先发也当过中继，见多识广，但只打过六场季后赛。
当他周四出现在罗杰斯中心时，洛伦岑与施耐德坐下来交谈，明确表示他愿意做任何事来帮助球队。
“洛伦岑说，‘真的，你想要什么都可以。如果你需要我，我今天就能投100球。你可以试着让我累垮，但那不会奏效，’”施耐德说。
这意味短期内他将担任牛棚角色，但如果洛伦岑能留下，他未来的角色可能与 Jameson Taillon 有关。蓝鸟队周三刚在对皇家队的比赛中成功实施了牛棚日计划，但在塔伊隆周五为三A水牛城队进行康复先发之后，他们愿意让他在下次轮换时回到先发轮值。
这仍然是首要计划，但如果塔伊隆需要另一次康复先发，或者先发轮值出现其他问题——这已经变得很常见——那么洛伦岑为蓝鸟队提供了另一层先发深度。

items.titleEn: Blue Jays hear it from home fans during lopsided loss to Royals
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Clinging to life in the AL Wild Card race, Thursday night couldn’t have been further from what the Blue Jays needed.
The 13-2 loss to the Royals dropped them to 3 1/2 games behind the Guardians, who had the night off, for the final spot.
This is what mattered most:
1. A low point in the seasonThe home crowd was already quiet heading into the sixth, then it completely fell apart.

Simeon Woods Richardson couldn’t find an out, with lasers shooting back the other way over and over again. Each time, the boos from the home crowd grew a bit louder. Toronto isn’t known as a baseball market that’s vocal in this way or hard on its own players, but in so many ways, Thursday’s loss felt different.

“For one, I understand. The fans are coming out every single night, which we love and appreciate,” manager John Schneider said. “There’s no better fans in the sport. That’s evident, the support we have from coast to coast. They’re entitled to their opinion. When you’re getting your ass kicked pretty good, they’re allowed to have their opinion. We love their support every night.”

That inning captured the dark side of this season so unfortunately well. With a gassed bullpen already needed after starter Spencer Arrighetti went four innings -- and an offense that hadn’t done a thing -- Woods Richardson had to wear it.
Every night, the Blue Jays pack over 40,000 fans into Rogers Centre. Every night, those fans hope to see the spark that launches a turnaround, but Thursday’s loss felt like a step backwards.

2. Nothing is going right for GuerreroMore batting practice and less of it, hitting off a tee and hitting outdoors, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has tried all of it lately. Still, nothing has unlocked him. There’s been no grand revelation.

“He’s been looking for something for a while now,” Schneider said. “He’s been doing a lot of work. I think it’s always good, when you’re looking for something, to try new things. He’s hit outside early a couple of times, but he’s looking for something to click and looking for something to hold onto and carry forward.”

It’s Schneider’s job to manage Guerrero as a person, not just a player. He’s been with Guerrero for nearly a decade now, back to their early days in the Minor Leagues together. He knows what makes Guerrero tick, but also what challenges him most. Schneider joked that he and the players can be good at “lying” sometimes, telling you they’re having a great day when they’re truly not, and he’s been working on that with Guerrero. ​

“He’s good at saying, ‘No, I’m good,’” Schneider said. “You have to keep asking him and break down that wall a little bit. The more you can be open and honest -- meaning him -- it probably makes it a little bit easier to get out of.”
The Blue Jays have 27 games remaining, but just 12 at home. Guerrero still hasn’t hit a home run at Rogers Centre this season, and he’s running out of time.

3. Arrighetti’s return is still a work in progressArrighetti is trying to figure this out on the fly, which isn’t an enviable position. He was traded from the Astros, an organization he was extremely comfortable with, and rehabbed a nerve issue in his right foot before returning to the big leagues last week with his new team. He’s still ramping up his workload and doing it in big league games now, but the Blue Jays no longer have the luxury of patience.
“There’s a lot going on,” Arrighetti said. “I’m still trying to establish myself as a Blue Jay. We’re trying to make a push and I’m trying to make some tweaks. There’s a lot.

“It makes your head spin some days. Other days, you’re convinced that you’ve finally found it. I think that’s the beauty of baseball. There’s always little things going on in the background and I handle it just by taking this one day at a time.”

Arrighetti allowed a leadoff homer, which set the tone for four innings of four-run ball (three earned). He got up to 79 pitches, which should leave him close to a “normal” workload his next time out, but that’s the lone bright spot from the evening.

The Blue Jays’ offense continues to put a strain on this pitching staff, demanding that it be nearly perfect to stay in games. For a pitcher like Arrighetti, who’s battling more than just the opposing lineup, that makes this game more challenging than it should be.
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟主场惨败 球迷嘘声不断
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟主场惨败皇家（13-2），球迷嘘声四起；Guerrero低迷，Arrighetti仍在适应。
bodyZh: 多伦多——蓝鸟仍在美联外卡争夺中艰难求生，但周四晚上的结果与他们的需求相去甚远。
这场13-2的失利让蓝鸟在最后一个外卡席位的争夺中落后当晚休战的守护者3.5个胜场。
以下是最重要的几点：
1. 赛季低谷 进入第六局时，主场球迷已经安静下来，随后局面彻底崩溃。
Simeon Woods Richardson 迟迟找不到出局方法，对方的击球一次又一次如激光般反向飞来。每一次，主场球迷的嘘声都变得更加响亮。多伦多并不是一个以这种方式喧闹或苛待自家球员的棒球市场，但从很多方面来看，周四的失利感觉有所不同。
“首先，我理解他们。球迷们每晚都会到场支持我们，我们喜爱并感激这一点，”主教练 John Schneider 说，“这项运动中没有比这更好的球迷了。我们得到的支持遍及全国，这显而易见。他们有权拥有自己的看法。当你被打得相当狼狈时，他们当然可以发表意见。我们每晚都热爱他们的支持。”
那一局不幸地完美展现了本赛季的阴暗面。先是先发投手 Spencer Arrighetti 只投了四局，牛棚已然精疲力竭，进攻端又毫无作为，Woods Richardson 只能默默承受。
每晚，蓝鸟都会在 Rogers Centre 吸引超过4万名球迷。每晚，这些球迷都希望看到点燃逆转的火花，但周四的失利感觉像是倒退了一步。
2. Guerrero 诸事不顺 近来，Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 尝试了增加或减少打击练习、用发球座打击以及在室外打击。尽管如此，他仍未找到打开局面的方法，也谈不上突破。
“他寻找状态已经有一段时间了，”Schneider 说，“他做了大量的工作。我觉得当你在寻找答案时，尝试新事物总是好的。他几次在早上进行户外打击，但他希望找到那个能激活自己的点，并紧紧抓住它带向前。”
Schneider 的职责在于管理 Guerrero 这个人，而不仅仅是球员。他与 Guerrero 相处了近十年，可以追溯到他们一起在小联盟的早期时光。他知道什么能让 Guerrero 保持活力，也知道什么最让他感到困扰。Schneider 开玩笑说，他和球员们有时很擅长“撒谎”，告诉你他们今天状态很好，但实际上并非如此，他一直在与 Guerrero 就这一点进行沟通。
“他擅长说‘不，我没事’，”Schneider 说，“你必须不断问他，打破那堵墙。你越是能开放和诚实——指他自己——也许就越容易走出来。”
蓝鸟本赛季还剩27场比赛，但只有12场在主场。Guerrero 本赛季还没有在 Rogers Centre 打出过本垒打，他的时间已经不多了。
3. Arrighetti 的回归仍在进行中 Arrighetti 还在边打边摸索解决办法，这并非令人羡慕的处境。他从太空人队被交易而来，那是一支他非常适应的球队，他右脚有神经问题，进行康复治疗后上周才随新东家重返大联盟。他仍在逐步增加投球量，而且是在大联盟比赛中进行，但蓝鸟队已经没有慢慢等待的资本了。
“有很多事情在发生，”Arrighetti 说，“我仍在努力确立自己作为蓝鸟球员的身份。我们正在冲刺，我也在尝试做一些调整。有很多。”
“有时这会让你头晕目眩。有时你又确信自己终于找到了答案。我认为这就是棒球的美妙之处。总有一些不起眼的事情在背后发生，而我只是一天一天地面对。”
Arrighetti 让对手首名打者轰出本垒打，这为四局丢四分（三分自责）的比赛定下了基调。他投了79球，这应该让他下一次先发接近“正常”的投球量，但这是当晚唯一的亮点。
蓝鸟的进攻继续给投手群施加压力，要求他们几乎完美才能让球队留在比赛中。对于像 Arrighetti 这样不仅要面对对方打线，还要应对自身状况的投手来说，这让比赛变得比原本更加艰难。
