items.titleEn: Assessing the state of the AL Wild Card race
bodyEn: Technically, there are 10 teams in the mix for three spots in the American League Wild Card race. But with the Red Sox and Yankees occupying the top two spots by a wide margin, the “race” really comes down to this: eight teams are vying for one spot, and, interestingly, all are hovering around the .500 mark, or are slightly below it.

It’s been that kind of year, where a bevy of teams that have struggled more than they’ve succeeded are still making a push. Mathematically, they’re all very much in this race, and with approximately 30 games remaining in the regular season, all it would take is one good week to pull away from the pack.

So let’s dive in. Among the AL teams fighting for that third Wild Card spot are the Guardians, Blue Jays, Twins, Orioles, Mariners and Tigers, with the Astros and Rangers also in the mix for both the AL West lead and Wild Card positioning.
Based on strength of schedule, how realistic would it be for your team to pull away from the pack?

Brian McTaggart, Astros beat reporter: The Astros (66-67) weren’t able to take advantage of a soft spot in their schedule, going 3-6 in a homestand last week against the Mariners, Angels and A’s to fall back to .500. Their remaining schedule is much tougher, with series at the Phillies and Rays and home series against the White Sox, D-backs and Braves. Houston is 24-14 against teams that were at .500 or above.

Kennedi Landry, Rangers beat reporter: The Rangers have the 10th-hardest remaining strength of schedule, including nine against teams they are battling against in the hunt: the Mariners, Blue Jays and Twins. Texas is 25-32 against teams at .500 and above and 41-35 against teams below .500. The remaining schedule is split almost evenly between those in contention and those out of it, but that doesn’t really matter for this Rangers team, which has not exactly done well against teams it’s “supposed” to beat over the last month, including a 2-5 road trip between Anaheim and Oakland earlier this month. The road to the postseason will have to include winning games they are meant to win.

Tim Stebbins, Guardians beat reporter: The Guardians entered Wednesday with the third-easiest remaining strength of schedule (.471) in MLB. They have every opportunity to pull away in this race, and they have recently been capitalizing on a light stretch of schedule. Cleveland has gone 8-1 over the past week against the Giants, Rockies and Angels. Going forward, the Guardians’ destiny is in their own hands. They will open September with 16 straight games against the Blue Jays, Tigers, Orioles, Twins and White Sox.
However, don’t discount the Guards in the AL Central race quite yet. They sit just 2 1/2 games behind the White Sox.

Keegan Matheson, Blue Jays beat reporter: The Blue Jays don’t have a daunting schedule, but are they really the team that’s going to reel off the biggest hot streak from this group? Their longest winning streak this season is four games. Playing slightly above .500 the rest of the way is certainly in the cards, but this tight race is going to be won by a team that goes on a true streak. Something would need to change quickly with Toronto’s offense for that to be possible.

Matthew Leach, Twins beat reporter: Well, the question specifies “based on schedule,” and based on schedule, the Twins have the opportunity. It’s one of the weaker run-ins of any team, with series against the plummeting Tigers and noncontending Angels and Giants mixed with matchups against the more daunting White Sox, Yankees and Guardians. This has been a pretty good team against the AL and a bad one against the NL, and Minnesota’s only remaining Interleague games are in San Francisco. That’s good news.

Jake Rill, Orioles beat reporter: The O’s are in a great position to rack up some wins over the next week, as the next two stops on their three-city, nine-game road trip are West Sacramento and Denver, where they’ll face the worst team in the AL (A’s) and the worst team in the NL (Rockies). But the rest of September will be much tougher, as the O’s will play three teams currently in playoff spots (Brewers, Yankees, Red Sox) and two in this race (Guardians and Blue Jays). So, there are some challenges lying ahead for Baltimore.

Daniel Kramer, Mariners beat reporter: This might be the leading reason why the Mariners are in such a prime position to think even bigger than the Wild Card -- and instead secure the division. Seattle has had the Majors’ most difficult schedule in August, with all nine of its series against teams either in postseason position or in close proximity. That included a 4-2 homestand against the Cubs and Phillies, two sure bets to play in October. Per Elias, it was MLB’s most difficult schedule in August, but the Mariners have the easiest remaining schedule once the calendar flips, with a combined 17 games against the Angels, A’s and Rockies. If they reach September within just a few games of first place, they’ll probably be the favorites to claim the AL West crown.

Jason Beck, Tigers beat reporter: The good news for Detroit is a stretch of games against other teams in the race starting next week: three games in Minnesota, four games in Cleveland, then three more against the Twins in Detroit. The Tigers also have a three-game trip to Toronto the following week. If they get hot again like they were just a few weeks ago, they can get back in a good position in a hurry. But they have to do it with an injury-depleted lineup and a rotation that, while very talented, no longer has Tarik Skubal or Casey Mize. But as Max Clark pointed out, Detroit’s odds are better now than they were two years ago before it came out of nowhere to take a Wild Card spot. In fairness, it’s hard to get much lower than the 0.2% chance the Tigers had in ‘24 without being eliminated.

Mark Feinsand, senior national reporter: I like the Blue Jays’ chances based on their schedule. Toronto has a series or two remaining against most of the teams it’s battling for this spot: Mariners (three games), Guardians (three), Orioles (six), Tigers (three) and Rangers (three). The rest of the schedule is weak, with the Royals (four), Athletics (three) and Reds (three) on the docket. They’re done with the Yankees, Red Sox and Rays, and if the Blue Jays can pull themselves together -- a big if, of course -- they can sneak into the playoffs to give themselves a chance to defend their AL crown.
What has been the biggest hurdle for your team in the last several weeks that has prevented them from making a push?

McTaggart: Yordan Alvarez, the AL MVP frontrunner and AL Player of the Month in July, has only one homer in August, and leadoff hitter Jeremy Peña has cooled off in August as well. When those two aren’t hitting like they did in the first half, the offense gets stagnant. Houston has gone 13 consecutive games (since Aug. 10) without a starting pitcher finishing six innings, which has put a heavy load on a bullpen that’s been among the Majors’ best since May 1.

Landry: Everything? Where to start? The health of key players (Corey Seager, Wyatt Langford, Josh Jung), the regression of a rotation that was MLB’s best in 2025 and a dramatically inconsistent offense all have a hand in the Rangers’ inability to go on a run and grab hold of the division. It also hasn’t helped that the depth at the upper levels of the Minors has not provided capable reinforcements on either end of the ball.

Stebbins: Things have evened out of late, but before this recent surge, it was the inability to play a complete game. When the Guardians pitched well, their offense was quiet. When they were productive at the plate, their pitching struggled. It was uncanny. The pitching staff has been the club’s backbone this season and has continually masked the offense’s collective struggles. It’s unrealistic to expect that for 162 games, though.

Matheson: If Vladimir Guerrero Jr. could wake up tomorrow as the 2025 postseason version of himself, you could call the race. With peak Vladdy, the Blue Jays are the best team in the race, but that just isn’t their reality. Without him, this is a singles-hitting team that has struggled to hit with runners in scoring position, which is a dangerous combination. Toronto is pitching well enough despite its injuries and is playing elite defense, but the offense continues to hold the club back from making a true run.

Leach: It’s a lot of things, but it starts with the struggles and then absence of Joe Ryan. The right-hander earned an All-Star berth with a brilliant first half, but he hasn’t been right since then, struggling out of the break before landing on the IL. The Twins entered the season with a ton of starting-pitching depth, but it’s been stretched to the brink with a string of injuries, and with Ryan not setting the tone, the starting five has searched for form. That in turn has taxed the bullpen, which was fortified at the Deadline but has scuffled a bit lately.

Rill: Offensive inconsistency, which is a bit surprising, considering many thought pitching would be the Orioles’ weak point in 2026. Instead, the starting rotation has been great and the bullpen has been solid enough. Meanwhile, the bats are too up and down. Baltimore’s lineup has so much potential, but there are too many times when it gets shut down completely. It hasn’t helped that Gunnar Henderson is having the least productive season of his MLB career.

Kramer: It’s been a maddening four months because Seattle’s struggles have been so widespread. It starts with the offense, which has featured an all-time drop-off from Cal Raleigh (though he’s legitimately starting to heat up). He’s been a big reason why the Mariners experienced MLB’s third-largest drop-off in slugging percentage. Yet it’s also been the volatility within their rotation, which has arguably the AL’s biggest upside but has also been susceptible to unpredictable clunkers -- and across the entire group. But the entire roster is starting to collectively put it all together, which is why they’ve won seven of their past 11.

Beck: The Tigers were able to withstand losing Skubal and Mize at the Trade Deadline thanks to Jacob Melton and Jackson Jobe. But Riley Greene’s right hamstring injury, coinciding with a deep slump from Dillon Dingler and continued injury woes for Kerry Carpenter, has stalled what had been a rejuvenated Detroit offense. Kevin McGonigle and Colt Keith have taken on the burden of left-handed-hitting run producers, and neither is really that kind of hitter at this point. Brett Callahan jumped from holding his own at Triple-A Toledo to batting fifth, sixth and even leadoff in his first month in the Majors, and that’s a tough route for a 13th-round Draft pick in 2023 who hadn’t played above High-A ball until this year. And the bullpen is still a mess.

Feinsand: I’ll stick with the Jays here since I have my pick: They need Vladdy to be Vladdy. He hasn’t been himself all year -- he hasn’t hit a home run at home this season! -- but if he can find his classic form, it will be an enormous addition down the stretch. Pitching hasn’t been the problem -- Toronto ranks second in the AL in ERA over the past month -- but its numbers with runners in scoring position have been bad. Clutch hits are a must if the team wants to play into October.
Give us a “pitch” how your team could win the Wild Card -- what positive signs have you seen that suggest they could get hot at the right time?

McTaggart: Alvarez is still the best hitter in the Majors and he could be poised for a big push entering the final month of the regular season, especially with a chance to win the AL Triple Crown. Peña is starting to show signs of coming out of his slump, and Daulton Varsho -- acquired at the Trade Deadline from the Blue Jays -- has settled into his new surroundings and is looking more comfortable at the plate. If they can find some consistent starting pitching, they could make the postseason.

Landry: Seager is back and he has the ability to carry a team. The franchise shortstop has endured three injured-list stints this season, two for nagging back issues and one with a concussion. And when he was healthy, he wasn’t exactly firing on all cylinders either. At the time of his most recent activation on July 31, Seager had hit just .182 with 10 home runs, six doubles, 25 RBIs and 28 walks in his 51 games. But he’s looked more like himself this month. In August, he’s slashing .305/.380/.476 with three home runs, five doubles and nine RBIs.

Stebbins: The Guardians’ offense has been inconsistent at best for most of the season. It has been much more productive this month. Through July, Cleveland had a collective .231/.310/.369 slash line and ranked 29th in MLB in runs scored (432). In August, the Guardians are eighth in runs (110) and have slashed .267/.343/.385. Trade Deadline acquisitions Jo Adell and Nathaniel Lowe have lengthened the lineup. Steven Kwan has enjoyed a dramatic in-season turnaround, and José Ramírez may be finding himself as he gets further removed from his left hamate surgery. Sustaining that production is the biggest key.

Matheson: Manager John Schneider has pointed to the “law of averages” often this year, which essentially suggests that it can’t get much worse. That’s not the most inspiring take, but there’s something to it. The Blue Jays have dealt with a stunning number of pitching injuries and have lived with Guerrero Jr.’s OPS below .700 all season. He’s homered just seven times. Despite all of this, Toronto is still part of this race, so the bar isn’t high here. Some timelier hitting could quickly flip this for the Blue Jays and they face many of these contenders down the stretch before finishing at home against the Reds. Their schedule is giving them every possible opportunity to get back into this.

Leach: They can hit. Even with Byron Buxton potentially headed back to the injured list, this is a deep lineup that has been productive most of the season. The way this comes together, if it does, is the offense regains its first-half form, Taj Bradley steps up and pitches like a No. 1, the rest of the rotation finds an upswing, and the reconfigured bullpen pitches like it’s capable. The thing is, every unit of this team has at some point looked good enough. It’s a matter of lining those up at the same time.

Rill: It still feels possible for the O’s to make a run, largely because of their starting pitching and the play of Pete Alonso, who has been everything he was expected to be upon signing a five-year, $155 million deal this past offseason. Alonso has been carrying the offense of late, but there has been some encouraging play from others, as well. If the Orioles keep pitching well, Alonso continues to be a driving force and some injury reinforcements help -- namely utility man Blaze Alexander, who was among the club’s top hitters before fracturing his left hand on July 12 -- there’s still a path to the postseason.

Kramer: It’s threefold -- 1) that they’re starting to click, 2) are doing so within striking distance and 3) as the schedule gets much more favorable. If Raleigh’s resurgence is legitimate, it could be seismic. Because when this offense can get any traction, Seattle has a good chance to win any given game. The Mariners are 47-18 when scoring at least four runs compared to 17-52 when plating three or fewer.

Beck: The Tigers have a combination of players who remember their 2024 charge into the playoffs out of a similar hole, and rookies who don’t know any better to think they shouldn’t be able to do it again. Greene should be back soon along with Matt Vierling. Carpenter has a chance to get back. And the rotation is still plenty good with Melton and Jobe at the top. They need a LOT of things to go right, but with so many matchups left against fellow contenders, one more hot streak could get them back in position.

Feinsand: The Guardians and Blue Jays have the pitching to make a run, which is what we’ve seen during their recent winning streak. Those two teams also face the weakest schedules down the stretch based on opponents' winning percentages, so their three-game set in Cleveland next week could be the determining factor in this race when all is said and done.
items.titleZh: 美联外卡竞争形势评估
items.summaryZh: 美联外卡争夺激烈，红袜洋基领先，八队争最后一个名额。
bodyZh: 严格来说，有10支球队在竞争美联外卡赛的3个名额。但由于红袜和洋基大幅领先占据前两席，这场“争夺战”实际上变成了：八支球队争夺一个席位，有趣的是，这些球队的胜率都徘徊在五成左右或略低于五成。
今年就是这样的一年，许多困境多于成功的球队仍在努力追赶。从数学上讲，他们都还有很大机会，常规赛还剩大约30场比赛，只需一周表现出色就能脱颖而出。
那么让我们深入探讨。在竞争第三个外卡席位的美国联盟球队中，有守护者、蓝鸟、双城、金莺、水手和老虎，而太空人和游骑兵也同时参与美联西区榜首和外卡位置的争夺。
根据赛程强度，你所报道的球队有多大可能脱颖而出？
Brian McTaggart（太空人随队记者）：太空人（66胜67负）未能利用赛程中一段轻松时期，上周主场系列赛对阵水手、天使和运动家只打出3胜6负，胜率回落至五成。剩余赛程要艰难得多，将客场对阵费城人和光芒，主场对阵白袜、响尾蛇和勇士。休斯敦对阵胜率五成及以上球队的战绩为24胜14负。

Kennedi Landry（游骑兵随队记者）：游骑兵剩余赛程难度排名联盟第10，其中九场比赛要对阵正在争夺外卡的球队：水手、蓝鸟和双城。得克萨斯对阵胜率五成及以上球队的战绩为25胜32负，对阵五成以下为41胜35负。剩余赛程中，与竞争者和非竞争者的对决几乎各占一半，但这支游骑兵队其实并不在乎这一点，因为他们本应击败的球队在过去一个月里表现并不好，包括本月初在阿纳海姆和奥克兰之间的客场之旅只取得2胜5负。通往季后赛之路必须包含赢得那些理应赢下的比赛。
Tim Stebbins（守护者随队记者）：守护者进入周三时，剩余赛程难度为大联盟第三低（对手胜率.471）。他们完全有机会在这场争夺中脱颖而出，而且最近一直在利用一段轻松的赛程。克利夫兰在过去一周对阵巨人、洛矶和天使打出8胜1负。展望未来，守护者的命运掌握在自己手中。他们将以连续16场比赛开启九月份，对手分别是蓝鸟、老虎、金莺、双城和白袜。
不过，在美联中区竞争中，现在还不能低估守护者。他们落后白袜仅两场半。
Keegan Matheson（蓝鸟随队记者）：蓝鸟的赛程并不艰难，但他们真的会成为这一组中打出最长连胜的球队吗？他们本赛季最长连胜是四场。剩余赛程略微高于五成胜率当然是可能的，但这场胶着的争夺将由一支真正打出连胜的球队赢得。要想做到这一点，多伦多的进攻需要迅速做出改变。
Matthew Leach（双城随队记者）：这个问题具体提到‘基于赛程’，从赛程来看，双城有机会。他们的收尾阶段赛程是各队中最轻松的之一，将对阵状态下滑的老虎以及无缘季后赛的天使和巨人，同时还要面对更强大的白袜、洋基和守护者。这支球队对阵美联球队时相当不错，对阵国联球队时表现糟糕，而明尼苏达仅剩的跨联盟比赛是在旧金山。这是个好消息。
Jake Rill（金莺随队记者）：金莺处于有利位置，未来一周有望累积胜场，因为他们这次三城九场客场之旅的下一站是西萨克拉门托和丹佛，将面对美联最差的球队（运动家）和国联最差的球队（洛矶）。但九月剩余赛程将艰难得多，因为金莺将对阵目前处于季后赛席位的三支球队（酿酒人、洋基、红袜）以及这场争夺中的两支球队（守护者和蓝鸟）。因此，巴尔的摩前方有一些挑战。

Daniel Kramer（水手随队记者）：这可能是水手处于优势地位、甚至可以考虑比外卡更远目标——直接锁定分区冠军的主要原因。西雅图在八月份遭遇了大联盟最艰难的赛程，九个系列赛全部对阵处于季后赛位置或接近季后赛位置的球队。其中包括对阵小熊和费城人的主场系列赛取得4胜2负，这两队几乎确定会出现在十月的比赛中。据Elias统计，这是大联盟八月份最艰难的赛程，但日历翻到九月后，水手拥有最轻松的剩余赛程，合计17场对阵天使、运动家和洛矶。如果他们进入九月时与榜首只差几场，他们可能会成为美联西区冠军的热门。

Jason Beck（老虎随队记者）：对底特律来说，好消息是从下周开始将有一系列对阵竞争球队的比赛：三场在明尼苏达，四场在克利夫兰，然后在底特律再战三场双城。老虎在下下周还有一次前往多伦多的三场客场之旅。如果他们能像几周前那样再次火热起来，就能迅速回到有利位置。但他们必须依靠伤病缠身的阵容和一套虽然很有天赋但已没有Tarik Skubal或Casey Mize的轮值来完成。但正如Max Clark指出的，底特律现在的几率比两年前它在毫无征兆地抢下外卡席位之前要好。公平地说，在未被淘汰的情况下，很难比老虎在2024年当时的0.2%概率更低。
Mark Feinsand（资深全国记者）：基于赛程，我看好蓝鸟的机会。多伦多与大多数争夺这个席位的球队还剩一个或两个系列赛：水手（三场）、守护者（三场）、金莺（六场）、老虎（三场）和游骑兵（三场）。剩余赛程较弱，还有皇家（四场）、运动家（三场）和红人（三场）。他们已经和洋基、红袜和光芒交手完毕，如果蓝鸟能够振作起来——当然，这是个大前提——他们可以悄悄溜进季后赛，从而有机会卫冕美联冠军。
过去几周，你所报道的球队最大的障碍是什么，导致他们无法发起冲击？
McTaggart：Yordan Alvarez，这位美联MVP热门人选和七月美联月度最佳球员，在八月仅打出一记本垒打，而首棒打者Jeremy Peña在八月也状态降温。当这两人不像上半季那样击球时，进攻就会停滞。休斯敦已连续13场比赛（自8月10日起）没有先发投手投完六局，这给牛棚带来了沉重负担，而牛棚自5月1日以来一直是大联盟最好的之一。
Landry：一切？从何说起？关键球员的健康（Corey Seager、Wyatt Langford、Josh Jung）、2025年大联盟最佳轮值的退步，以及极度不稳定的进攻，都导致游骑兵无法打出连胜并掌控分区。小联盟高级别体系的深度未能提供攻防两端的合格替补，也于事无补。
Stebbins：最近情况有所好转，但在这一波势头之前，球队一直无法打出完整的比赛。当守护者投球出色时，进攻端却沉寂。当他们在打击上有所产出时，投球又陷入困境。这真是诡异。投手群是球队本赛季的脊梁，一直掩盖着进攻端的集体低迷。不过，指望这种表现在162场比赛中持续是不现实的。
Matheson：如果Vladimir Guerrero Jr.明天醒来能变成2025年季后赛版本的自己，这场争夺就可以提前结束了。有巅峰状态的Vladdy，蓝鸟就是这场争夺中最好的球队，但那并不是他们的现实。没有他，这就是一支单打型球队，在得点圈有人时打击挣扎，这是一个危险的组合。多伦多尽管有伤病，但投球表现足够好，防守也是精英级别，但进攻端继续拖累球队，使其无法真正起飞。
Leach：原因很多，但首先是Joe Ryan的状态挣扎以及随后的缺阵。这位右投手凭借出色的上半季入选全明星，但自那以后一直不在状态，休赛期后表现挣扎，最终进入伤病名单。双城本赛季开始时拥有大量先发投手深度，但一连串伤病将其逼到了极限，由于Ryan未能定下基调，先发五虎一直在寻找状态。这反过来又使牛棚不堪重负，牛棚在交易截止日得到了补强，但最近有些挣扎。
Rill：进攻不稳定，这有点令人意外，因为许多人原本以为投球是金莺2026年的弱点。相反，先发轮值表现出色，牛棚也足够稳固。与此同时，打线起伏太大。巴尔的摩的阵容潜力巨大，但有太多次被完全压制。Gunnar Henderson正经历他大联盟生涯最低产的赛季，这也无济于事。
Kramer：这四个月令人抓狂，因为西雅图的挣扎无处不在。首先是进攻端，Cal Raleigh出现了历史级别的下滑（虽然他确实开始回暖）。他是水手长打率下滑幅度居大联盟第三的重要原因。此外，轮值内部也不稳定，这个轮值可以说是美联上限最高的，但也容易莫名其妙地被打爆——而且是全组如此。但整个阵容开始逐渐磨合，这就是他们过去11场赢下7场的原因。

Beck：老虎能够在交易截止日失去Skubal和Mize后依然撑住，要感谢Jacob Melton和Jackson Jobe。但Riley Greene的右腿筋伤势，加上Dillon Dingler的深度低迷和Kerry Carpenter持续的伤病问题，让底特律原本复苏的进攻停滞不前。Kevin McGonigle和Colt Keith承担了左打跑垒者的重担，但两人目前都不是那种类型的打者。Brett Callahan从在3A托莱多站稳脚跟，到升上大联盟第一个月就担任第五棒、第六棒甚至首棒，这对一位2023年第13轮选秀、今年之前从未在高级A以上级别打球的人来说是一条艰难的路。牛棚依然一团糟。
Feinsand：既然我选择了蓝鸟，我就坚持这个观点：他们需要Vladdy做回Vladdy。他整年都不在状态——本赛季他在主场还没有打出过本垒打！——但如果他能找回经典状态，那将是收尾阶段的一大助力。投球不是问题——多伦多过去一个月的自责分率排名美联第二——但得点圈有人时的数据很糟糕。如果球队想打到十月，关键安打必不可少。
请说说你所报道的球队如何赢得外卡——你看到了哪些积极迹象，表明他们可能在正确的时候状态火热？
McTaggart：Alvarez仍然是大联盟最好的打者，他有望在常规赛最后一个月发起强势冲击，尤其是在有机会赢得美联三冠王的情况下。Peña开始显露出摆脱低迷的迹象，Daulton Varsho——在交易截止日从蓝鸟换来——已经适应了新环境，在打击区看起来更自在了。如果他们能找到稳定的先发投球，他们就能打进季后赛。

Landry：Seager回来了，他有能力扛起整支球队。这位球队基石游击手本赛季三度进入伤病名单，两次是因为背部老伤，一次是脑震荡。而且当他健康时，也并非火力全开。在7月31日最近一次激活时，Seager在51场比赛中打击率仅.182，有10支本垒打、6支二垒安打、25分打点和28次保送。但他本月看起来更像个自己了。八月份，他打击三围为.305/.380/.476，有3支本垒打、5支二垒安打和9分打点。

Stebbins：守护者的进攻在本赛季大部分时间里充其量只能说是不稳定。本月则高效得多。截至七月，克利夫兰整体打击三围为.231/.310/.369，得分（432分）排名大联盟第29位。八月，守护者得分（110分）排名第八，打击三围为.267/.343/.385。交易截止日的引援Jo Adell和Nathaniel Lowe延长了打线。Steven Kwan经历了一波戏剧性的赛季中段回暖，而José Ramírez随着左手钩骨手术恢复时间越久，可能也在找回状态。保持这种产出是最关键的一点。

Matheson：主教练John Schneider今年经常提到‘平均法则’，这基本上意味着情况不可能再糟了。这不是最鼓舞人心的说法，但确实有些道理。蓝鸟遭遇了数量惊人的投手伤病，而且整个赛季都在忍受Guerrero Jr.的OPS低于.700。他仅打出七支本垒打。尽管如此，多伦多仍然是这场争夺的一部分，所以门槛并不高。一些更及时的打击可以迅速改变蓝鸟的局面，他们在收尾阶段将面对许多竞争者，最后在主场对阵红人。他们的赛程给了他们一切可能的机会重新回到竞争中来。
Leach：他们能打。即使Byron Buxton可能回到伤病名单，这套阵容仍然深厚，本赛季大部分时间都很有产出。如果这一切能成真，那需要进攻端找回上半季的状态，Taj Bradley挺身而出，投出王牌级表现，轮值其他成员找到上升势头，重组后的牛棚发挥出应有实力。问题是，这支球队的每个部分都曾在某个时刻看起来足够好。关键是要让这些同时到位。

Rill：金莺仍然有望发起冲击，主要因为他们的先发投球和Pete Alonso的表现，后者在去年休赛期签下五年1.55亿美元合同后，表现完全符合预期。Alonso近来一直在扛起进攻，但其他球员也有一些令人鼓舞的表现。如果金莺继续投出好球，Alonso继续作为驱动力，并且一些伤兵增援能有所帮助——比如工具人Blaze Alexander，他在7月12日左手骨折前是球队最好的打者之一——那么仍有通往季后赛的道路。
Kramer：有三点——1）他们开始进入状态，2）他们在可触及的范围内做到这一点，3）赛程变得更有利。如果Raleigh的复苏是真实的，那可能是地震级的。因为当这支进攻端能够取得任何进展时，西雅图就有很大机会赢下任何一场比赛。水手得分至少4分时战绩为47胜18负，而得分3分或更少时仅为17胜52负。
Beck：老虎阵中既有记得2024年从类似困境中杀入季后赛的球员，也有不知天高地厚、认为他们还能再做到一次的菜鸟。Greene应该很快回归，Matt Vierling也会回来。Carpenter有机会复出。轮值仍然相当出色，Melton和Jobe领衔。他们需要很多事顺遂，但面对如此多与竞争者交手的机会，再一波火热状态就能让他们回到有利位置。
Feinsand：守护者和蓝鸟拥有发起冲击的投球实力，这正是我们在他们最近的连胜中所看到的。这两支球队在收官阶段也拥有基于对手胜率最弱的赛程，所以下周他们在克利夫兰的三场系列赛可能是这场争夺最终的决定性因素。

items.titleEn: Where does Cease stand in latest Pitcher Power Rankings?
bodyEn: If we've learned one thing heading into our 10th Starting Pitcher Power Rankings, it's this: There is no unseating The Miz.

Since our last poll earlier this month, the otherworldly Jacob Misiorowski has pitched to a 2.16 ERA with 31 strikeouts in 25 innings across four starts. That sort of performance certainly isn't going to unseat Misiorowski from the top spot. He'll climb the mound again on Thursday night against the Mets at Citi Field.
How do the rankings shake out behind The Miz? Here are the latest Starting Pitcher Power Rankings, as voted on by a panel of experts.
(All stats are through Tuesday’s games, unless otherwise noted.)

1. Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers (Last poll: 1)The Miz has held onto the top spot of these rankings for six consecutive polls, dating back to mid-June. He reached No. 1 for the first time a few days after his 15-strikeout one-hitter against the Phillies. Since then, Misiorowski has turned in a 2.17 ERA and a 38.5% strikeout rate over his past 10 starts. Both numbers are fantastic -- and also worse than his season averages (1.68 and 39.3%, respectively). That's how ridiculously dominant the 24-year-old flamethrower has been in 2026. In his most recent start, Misiorowski outdueled Chris Sale, ostensibly his strongest competition for the National League Cy Young Award, in a 2-1 Brewers win.

2. Cam Schlittler, Yankees (3)Dylan Cease took the No. 2 spot away from Schlittler in our last set of SP Power Rankings, but the Yanks' ace has regained it amid a three-start stretch with only three earned runs allowed, lowering his ERA to 2.16, second in MLB only to Misiorowski. Schlittler limited Cease's Blue Jays to one over six innings in his last time out while wearing "Star Wars" cleats. He has carved through the AL this season with a trio of fastballs, but the recent implementation of a curveball that can touch 90 mph could make Schlittler even nastier moving forward.

3. Dylan Cease, Blue Jays (2)One day after Schlittler tamed Toronto, Cease stepped to the mound in the Bronx and once again flirted with a no-hitter. He took a no-no into the sixth inning for the third time this season and kept it intact until a seventh-inning single en route to his eighth win. Cease has reached double-digit strikeouts in five of his past 10 starts, and he is pacing the the junior circuit with 209 K's and a 25.0% strikeout-minus-walk rate. This is his sixth consecutive season with 200 strikeouts; only five pitchers have had longer such streaks in MLB history.

4. Chris Sale, Braves (4)In the middle of his 16th season and at age 37, Sale is pitching some of the best ball of his career right now. Through six starts since the All-Star break, the left-hander has recorded 49 K's and only three walks. That stretch includes a 2.19 ERA, a 2.05 expected ERA and a skinny 0.76 FIP. Those last two numbers are the best since the break among qualified hurlers. Sale is creeping toward his ninth 200-K campaign. That would be the second-most seasons by any southpaw in MLB history, trailing only Randy Johnson.

5. Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies (7)Although Sánchez wasn't at his best in his most recent outing, he came into that start having permitted only three earned runs through four starts (23 innings) this month. Last year's NL Cy Young runner-up ranks fifth in the Majors with 194 K's and is sixth among qualified pitchers with a career-best 21.5% K-BB rate. He's on track to lead MLB for the second straight season in pitching bWAR (7.1) and is second to The Miz in fWAR (5.4).

6. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers (5)It’s fair to wonder if Yamamoto’s brilliance is overlooked these days, especially amid all the hoopla surrounding recently-acquired Tarik Skubal and the rehabbing Shohei Ohtani. But the right-hander is proving every bit as dominant as he was last season, when he finished third in NL Cy Young Award voting and almost single-handedly vaulted the Dodgers to a World Series title. Yamamoto’s 2.61 ERA is tied for the sixth lowest among qualified starting pitchers, and his .186 batting average against is third lowest. Just like last year, no one will want to face him come October.

7-T. Chase Burns, Reds (not ranked)Burns, the No. 2 pick in the 2024 Draft out of Wake Forest, is putting the finishing touches on a stellar first full season in the Majors. He has a top 10 ERA (2.77), FIP (3.11) and strikeout rate (28.9%) among qualified starters. What’s most impressive about Burns, though, is how he goes about all this. He is a true two-pitch pitcher, relying on a wipeout slider and a hoppy four-seam fastball that averages 97.6 mph. That sort of pitch mix is exceedingly rare in an era where pitchers are embracing broad arsenals. But Burns’ two pitches are so nasty – why would he throw anything else?

7-T. Jesús Luzardo, Phillies (9)It’s fair to wonder these days where Luzardo slots into the Phillies’ potential postseason rotation. Could he be their Game 2 starter, ahead of Zack Wheeler? That’s not a slight on Wheeler, arguably the best pitcher in baseball since he first put on a Phillies uniform. This is simply about how good Luzardo has been. After twirling seven scoreless innings in Seattle on Wednesday, the left-hander has a 2.11 ERA over his last 19 starts. That ranks third lowest in the Majors in that span -- which dates back to mid-May -- behind only Jacob Misiorowski and the Tigers' Troy Melton.

9. Drew Rasmussen, Rays (6)Tampa Bay's veteran righty is as consistent as they come. Don't believe us? This season, Rasmussen has a 2.95 ERA and a 144 ERA+ in 25 starts. For his career, the two-time All-Star has a 2.91 ERA with a 140 ERA+. This is simply what he does. With 140 1/3 innings under his belt, Rasmussen is also wading into uncharted territory. He seems poised to break his single-season high of 150 innings pitched, which he set just last season, as the Rays barrel toward the postseason.

10. Parker Messick, Guardians (not ranked)Messick is a whirling dervish on the mound, and hitters can't crack him. The rookie southpaw has allowed two runs or fewer in 19 of his 26 starts this season; only the Yankees' Cam Schlittler has more such outings this season. That's not the only similarity between Messick and Schlittler. Sure, Messick doesn't throw nearly as hard -- his 93.8 mph average fastball velocity is in the 38th percentile of MLB -- but his trio of fastballs are just as dominant. He has accrued the most run value on fastballs of any pitcher in the Majors this season, at plus-34 runs.
Others receiving votes: Tarik Skubal (Dodgers), Reid Detmers (Angels), Gavin Williams (Guardians), Cade Cavalli (Nationals), Sandy Alcantara (Marlins), Troy Melton (Tigers), Sonny Gray (Red Sox)
Voters: Theo DeRosa, Brent Maguire, Brian Murphy, Max Ralph, Manny Randhawa
items.titleZh: 先发投手实力榜：Cease 位列第三
items.summaryZh: 最新先发投手实力榜公布，Misiorowski 居首，Cease 排名第三。
bodyZh: 如果我们在进入第10期先发投手实力榜时学到了什么，那就是：没有人能撼动 The Miz 的王座。
自从本月早些时候的上一次投票以来，超凡脱俗的 Jacob Misiorowski 在四次先发中投了25局，自责分率2.16，送出31次三振。这样的表现当然不会让 Misiorowski 丢掉榜首位置。他将于周四晚上在花旗球场面对大都会时再次登板。
在 The Miz 之后，排名如何？以下是专家小组投票选出的最新先发投手实力榜。
（除非另有说明，所有数据均截至周二比赛结束。）

1. Jacob Misiorowski，酿酒人（上期排名：1）The Miz 自六月中旬以来已连续六期保持榜首。他在对阵费城人时投出15次三振的一安打比赛几天后首次升至第一。此后，Misiorowski 在过去10场先发中自责分率2.17，三振率38.5%。这两个数字都很出色——但也低于他本赛季的平均水平（分别为1.68和39.3%）。这就是这位24岁火球男在2026年的统治力有多么夸张。在最近一次先发中，Misiorowski 在酿酒人2-1战胜勇士的比赛中压制了 Chris Sale，后者显然是他争夺国联赛扬奖的最强对手。

2. Cam Schlittler，洋基（3）Dylan Cease 在上期实力榜中从 Schlittler 手中抢走了第二名，但洋基的王牌在连续三场先发中仅失3分自责分后重新夺回这一位置，将自责分率降至2.16，仅次于 Misiorowski 位列 MLB 第二。Schlittler 上一次先发穿着“星球大战”球鞋，六局只让 Cease 的蓝鸟得到一分。本赛季他用三种快速球撕碎了美国联盟，但最近加入的时速可达90英里的曲球可能会让 Schlittler 未来更加难缠。

3. Dylan Cease，蓝鸟（2）在 Schlittler 压制多伦多后的第二天，Cease 在布朗克斯登板，再次险些投出无安打比赛。他本赛季第三次将无安打比赛带入第六局，并在第七局被击出一支安打后才破功，最终拿下第八胜。Cease 在过去10场先发中有5场达到两位数三振，并以209次三振和25.0%的三振减保送率领跑美国联盟。这是他连续第六个赛季达到200次三振；MLB 历史上只有五位投手的连续赛季数比他更长。

4. Chris Sale，勇士（4）在职业生涯第16个赛季的中段，37岁的 Sale 目前正在投出职业生涯中最好的表现。全明星赛后六场先发中，这位左投手送出49次三振，仅3次保送。这段期间包括2.19的自责分率、2.05的预期自责分率和0.76的防守独立投球。后两项数据是休赛期后达标投手中最好的。Sale 正在逼近他职业生涯第九次单赛季200次三振。那将是 MLB 历史上左投手中第二多的赛季次数，仅次于 Randy Johnson。
5. Cristopher Sánchez，费城人（7）虽然 Sánchez 在最近一次出赛中没有处于最佳状态，但他在那场先发之前，本月四场先发（23局）仅失3分自责分。去年的国联赛扬奖亚军以194次三振排名大联盟第五，并以职业生涯最佳的21.5%三振减保送率在达标投手中排名第六。他有望连续第二个赛季领跑 MLB 的投手 bWAR（7.1），并在 fWAR（5.4）中仅次于 The Miz。

6. Yoshinobu Yamamoto，道奇（5）我们有理由怀疑山本由伸的出色表现如今是否被忽视，尤其是在最近引进的 Tarik Skubal 和正在康复中的大谷翔平引起诸多关注的情况下。但这位右投手正在证明自己与上赛季一样具有统治力——当时他在国联赛扬奖投票中排名第三，几乎以一己之力带领道奇夺得世界大赛冠军。山本由伸的2.61自责分率在达标先发投手中并列第六低，被打击率.186排名第三低。和去年一样，十月份没有人愿意面对他。

7-并列. Chase Burns，红人（未上榜）Burns 是2024年选秀大会来自维克森林大学的榜眼秀，正在为他在大联盟的第一个完整赛季画上圆满句号。在达标先发投手中，他的自责分率（2.77）、防守独立投球（3.11）和三振率（28.9%）均进入前十。不过，Burns 最令人印象深刻的是他做到这一切的方式。他是一名真正的两球种投手，依赖一颗横扫滑球和一颗平均时速97.6英里的上飘四缝线快速球。在投手们普遍采用多样化球种的时代，这种球种组合极为罕见。但 Burns 的两种球路如此犀利——他为什么要投其他球呢？

7-并列. Jesús Luzardo，费城人（9）如今我们有理由思考 Luzardo 在费城人潜在季后赛轮值中的位置。他能成为第二战先发，排在 Zack Wheeler 之前吗？这并不是对 Wheeler 的贬低，他或许是穿上费城人球衣后棒球界最好的投手。这仅仅说明 Luzardo 有多出色。周三在西雅图投出七局无失分后，这位左投手在过去19场先发中的自责分率仅为2.11。在这段时间——从五月中旬至今——他的自责分率在大联盟排名第三低，仅次于 Jacob Misiorowski 和老虎队的 Troy Melton。
9. Drew Rasmussen，光芒（6）坦帕湾的资深右投手一如既往地稳定。不信？本赛季 Rasmussen 在25场先发中自责分率2.95，ERA+为144。职业生涯中，这位两届全明星球员自责分率2.91，ERA+为140。这就是他的风格。Rasmussen 已经投了140 1/3局，正在涉足未知领域。他似乎有望打破自己上赛季创下的单赛季150局投球纪录，而光芒队正朝着季后赛冲刺。

10. Parker Messick，守护者（未上榜）Messick 在投手丘上像旋转的苦行僧，打者无法破解他。这位新秀左投手本赛季26场先发中有19场失分不超过两分；只有洋基队的 Cam Schlittler 本赛季有更多这样的表现。这不是 Messick 和 Schlittler 之间的唯一相似之处。当然，Messick 的球速远没有那么快——平均快速球时速93.8英里，处于 MLB 第38百分位——但他的三种快速球同样具有统治力。他本赛季在快速球上取得的跑垒价值是全大联盟最高的，达到+34分。
其他获得选票的投手：Tarik Skubal（道奇）、Reid Detmers（天使）、Gavin Williams（守护者）、Cade Cavalli（国民）、Sandy Alcantara（马林鱼）、Troy Melton（老虎）、Sonny Gray（红袜）
投票人：Theo DeRosa、Brent Maguire、Brian Murphy、Max Ralph、Manny Randhawa

items.titleEn: Fluharty a dark-horse stalwart for Blue Jays' bullpen
bodyEn: This story was excerpted from Keegan Matheson’s Blue Jays Beat newsletter. To read the full newsletter, click here. And subscribe to get it regularly in your inbox.
TORONTO -- Mason Fluharty will probably pitch tonight. Maybe tomorrow night, too. He pitches, pitches and pitches.
Fluharty’s 71 appearances lead Major League Baseball this season. He’s on track to clear 80 appearances, which has only been done by four relievers in total over the past five seasons.

Quietly, Fluharty has been one of the Blue Jays’ most important pitchers, a rock in the middle of a bullpen that’s evolved throughout the year. He’s underrated, but isn’t that a compliment for relievers? Unless you’re a closer, it’s rarely good news for a reliever to be part of the daily discourse among fans. Just like Tyler Rogers, Fluharty flies an inch under the radar, supremely reliable.
None of this is by accident. The 25-year-old Fluharty has built himself for this exact role, even if there have been some painful sacrifices along the way.

“I can’t be eating Taco Bell every night,” Fluharty said. “As much as I want to. Big Taco Bell guy. Honestly, it’s about being honest and telling [the staff] when I need a day. There was a point in the season where I was gassed, but I got over it pretty quickly. We have the best trainers in the league. They’re not running me out there for three innings, either. I might have the most appearances, but I probably have the least amount of innings. That’s just the life of a lefty.”

Fluharty’s got a point, and if he’d come into the league before the three-batter minimum, his numbers would be even more extreme. He’s pitched 53 2/3 innings, used against pockets of lineups where there are a couple of lefties or one big bat.
He’s dominated lefties, too, holding those hitters to a .159 average and .451 OPS. That’s nasty, even if Fluharty wants to downplay it.

“Maybe I’m not having the best ‘reliever season,' and I’m not Louis Varland. That’s pretty hard to beat,” Fluharty said, “but they trust me enough to where, if there’s a big spot and there’s a lefty coming up, they’re going to throw me. It doesn’t matter what day it is. They’re ready to get me in there and I’m always ready to answer their call. I’m just thankful they trust me. I’m going to keep answering that call."

This is a manager’s dream. Again, with Fluharty and Rogers being similar in this regard, every manager needs an “easy button." When in doubt, throw in Fluharty or Rogers. They’re both made of rubber and both can handle it.

Fluharty’s come to this so young, though. Last season, he made 66 appearances between Triple-A and the big leagues, but when we think of these ultra-durable relievers, it’s typically a more grizzled veteran like Rogers.

“He’s worked really hard to be a workhorse reliever,” Schneider said, “and he works to be available as much as he is. We’re talking about a two-pitch pitcher last year who has three now with the changeup. He does his homework really well, too. It’s nice to have that presence, especially from the left side in this league and this division. It sets a blueprint for younger guys. Hey, this is how we do it.”

Making Fluharty even friendlier to a manager is how quickly he can warm up. This is rarely talked about, but it matters, because it allows Schneider and Pete Walker to take their decisions down to the last moment without wasting relievers.
Fluharty can warm up with as few as four or five pitches, which is extremely rare. He calls it “a batter,” and he’s ready to rock.

“Everybody wants the ball. There’s no guy in that bullpen who doesn’t want the ball,” Fluharty said. “Everybody wants the ball and we want to help the team win. Our bullpen is a big part of us winning. I’m just waking up every day ready to take the ball.”

You need the right attitude for this job, too. Closers are a different type of human being altogether, thriving on the highest adrenaline that baseball has to offer, but the workhorse relievers tend to go one of two ways. You can have one like Rogers, who looks as calm on the mound as most people do sipping their morning coffee. Then, there’s Fluharty, who brings more of an edge but is wonderfully stubborn, never backing down from a challenge.
Varland gets the headlines, but Fluharty, over and over again, sets it up. If you don’t hear about him much, that just means he’s doing
items.titleZh: Fluharty 成蓝鸟牛棚黑马中坚
bodyZh: 本文摘自 Keegan Matheson 的 Blue Jays Beat 通讯。要阅读完整通讯，请点击此处。并订阅以定期在收件箱中接收。
多伦多——Mason Fluharty 今晚可能会上场投球，也许明晚也会。他投球、投球、再投球。
Fluharty 本赛季以 71 次出场领跑大联盟。他有望超过 80 次出场，而过去五个赛季总共只有四位后援投手做到过。
Fluharty 一直是蓝鸟最重要的投手之一，是本赛季不断演变的牛棚中的中流砥柱。他被低估了，但这对后援投手来说难道不是一种赞美吗？除非你是终结者，否则对于后援投手来说，成为球迷日常讨论的话题很少是什么好事。就像 Tyler Rogers 一样，Fluharty 几乎不引人注目，却极为可靠。
这一切并非偶然。25 岁的 Fluharty 为自己塑造了这样的角色，即使一路上做出了一些痛苦的牺牲。
"我不能每晚都吃 Taco Bell，" Fluharty 说。"虽然我很想。我是 Taco Bell 的忠实粉丝。说实话，关键在于诚实地告诉工作人员我需要休息一天。赛季中有一个阶段我感觉筋疲力尽，但我很快就恢复过来了。我们有联盟最好的训练师。他们也不会让我投三局。我可能出场次数最多，但我的局数可能最少。这就是左投的生活。"
Fluharty 说得有道理，如果他是在“至少面对三名打者”规则出台前进入联盟的，他的数据会更加极端。他已经投了 53 2/3 局，被用来对付打线片段中一两位左打者或一位重炮手。
他也完全压制了左打者，将他们的打击率限制在 .159，攻击指数 .451。这真的很厉害，即使 Fluharty 想轻描淡写。
"也许我打不出最好的‘后援投手赛季’，我也不是 Louis Varland。这很难比得上，" Fluharty 说，"但他们足够信任我，如果关键时刻有左打者上场，他们就会派我上场。不管是什么日子。他们准备好让我上场，我也随时准备响应他们的召唤。我只是感谢他们的信任。我会继续回应那种召唤。"
这是教练的梦想。同样，Fluharty 和 Rogers 在这方面很相似，每位教练都需要一个“轻松按钮”。犹豫不决时，就派上 Fluharty 或 Rogers。他们俩都像橡胶做的一样，都能扛住。
然而，Fluharty 这么年轻就做到了。上赛季，他在 3A 和大联盟之间总共出场 66 次，但当我们想到这些超耐用的后援投手时，通常会是像 Rogers 这样的老将。
"他为成为一名劳模型后援投手付出了很多努力，" Schneider 说，"他也努力让自己像现在这样随时可用。我们说的是去年只有两种球路的投手，现在有三种，加上变速球。他的功课也做得很好。有这样一个存在是很好的，尤其是在这个联盟和这个分区中的左投。它为年轻球员树立了一个蓝图。嘿，这就是我们做事的方式。"
让 Fluharty 对教练更友好的是他热身的速度。这一点很少被谈论，但它很重要，因为它让 Schneider 和 Pete Walker 可以把决定留到最后一刻，而不会浪费后援投手。
Fluharty 只需投四五球就能热身，这极为罕见。他称之为“一个打者”，然后他就准备好大干一场了。
"每个人都想要球。牛棚里没有人不想要球，" Fluharty 说。"每个人都想要球，我们都想帮助球队获胜。我们的牛棚是我们取胜的重要组成部分。我每天醒来就准备拿起球。"
这份工作需要正确的态度。终结者是完全不同类型的人，他们靠棒球带来的最高肾上腺素茁壮成长，但劳模型后援投手往往有两种类型。你可以拥有像 Rogers 这样的投手，他在投手丘上看起来像大多数人喝早晨咖啡一样平静。然后，还有 Fluharty，他更有棱角，但非常倔强，从不畏惧挑战。
Varland 成为了头条，但 Fluharty 一次又一次地铺路。如果你很少听到他的消息，那只能说明他在……

items.titleEn: Lukes redeems previous night's mistake with game-winning home run
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The Blue Jays have turned bullpen days into their own art forms.

They pulled it off again in Wednesday’s 3-0 win over the Royals at Rogers Centre, potentially the last time they’ll need to scramble before their rotation is full again. The win keeps the Blue Jays on pace with the Guardians for the final American League Wild Card spot, but that gap sits at three games now with a crowded field around them.
This is what mattered most:
1. Sweet redemption for Nathan Lukes

In Tuesday’s series opener, Nathan Lukes recorded the final out of the game trying to stretch a single into a double, completely unnecessary as the tying run was still on deck in Vladimir Guerrero Jr. It felt so out of character for Lukes, who is typically a fundamentally sound player, but it’s the byproduct of everyone trying to do just a bit too much with this offense struggling.
Less than 24 hours later, he made up for it.

“I talked to him today and, as only Lukey can, he said he was sorry,” said manager John Schneider. “I told him, ‘Dude, the most important game is tonight. Don’t worry about it.’ It’s pretty fitting that he had the big hit today.”
That apology featured a big hug for Schneider, too, and Lukes’ teammates felt it.

“There were a few guys that came up to me and said that I was going to come up big tonight just to make up for what happened,” Lukes said. “I guess you can't screw up baserunning if you just hit the ball over the fence. So this is great.”

Lukes launched a three-run shot in the bottom of the fourth, finally breaking this offense through after some missed opportunities earlier in the game. This was the exact type of pitch Lukes handles so well, too, a low breaking ball that he dropped down and used his legs to drive.

Now that everything has balanced out, we can get back to viewing Lukes as the player he truly is, which is a valuable piece of this team. Left-handed pitching has been awfully hard on Lukes this season, but he’s hit right-handed pitching well and should still be in the lineup against nearly every righty down the stretch.
2. Big pitch, big performance from Chad Dallas
The Blue Jays brought in Chad Dallas with the bases loaded, two outs and veteran Salvador Perez at the plate in the third inning. No pressure.

Dallas struck out Perez to escape the jam, though, including a couple of whiffs that weren’t even close. The right-hander gave the Blue Jays 2 2/3 innings of flawless relief, striking out four to get this bullpen game to the middle innings.

“I like his demeanor and I like his stuff,” Schneider said. “He knew exactly when he was coming in and he made big pitches. That’s a big strikeout there. That’s about as good as Chad has been. He did exactly what we needed him to.”

This was Dallas’ finest moment yet in the big leagues. It’s still surprising that this was only his fourth appearance of 2026 with the Blue Jays, given how many times he’s been up and down from Triple-A Buffalo, but it feels like he’s here to stay, especially with rosters expanding from 26 to 28 next week. His multi-inning length is extremely valuable right now, especially with Spencer Arrighetti still getting stretched out while the Blue Jays wait on the return of Jameson Taillon to fill the No. 5 spot.
3. Sean Keys an option to boost this lineup?
No. 6 prospect Sean Keys couldn’t produce much in his 12 big league games earlier this season, but what he’s done since returning to Triple-A Buffalo may soon earn him another look.
Keys now has 28 total home runs this season and is red hot for the Bisons. Again, with rosters about to expand, why not chase some extra power anywhere it can be found?

“He’s obviously in a really good stretch right now,” said Schneider. “We’ve talked about him and that offensive profile, how it would fit defensively. We’ll continue to talk about it. He’s playing some outfield this coming week in Triple-A.”

Keys has never played the outfield, but is expected to see some days in left field very soon. This team hasn’t shied away from spots like this in recent years, willing to wedge a hot hitter into a new position if it gets them in the lineup. At this point in the season, the Blue Jays need to chase upside and worry about the risks later.
items.titleZh: Lukes用制胜本垒打弥补前夜失误
bodyZh: 多伦多——蓝鸟将牛棚日变成了自己的艺术形式。
周三在罗杰斯中心3-0击败皇家队的比赛中，他们再次做到了这一点，这可能是他们在先发轮值恢复满员前最后一次需要临时拼凑投手。这场胜利让蓝鸟在美联外卡最后席位的争夺中与守护者保持同样步伐，但目前差距为三场，周围竞争者众多。
以下是本场最重要的内容：
1. Nathan Lukes的甜蜜救赎
在周二系列赛首战中，Nathan Lukes在比赛最后一人次试图将一垒安打跑成二垒安打而出局，当时追平分Vladimir Guerrero Jr.还未上场打击。这一举动完全没必要，对于通常基本功扎实的Lukes来说很反常，但这是球队进攻挣扎时每个人都想多做一点的副产品。
不到24小时后，他弥补了这一点。
“我今天和他谈过，只有Lukey会那样做，他向我道了歉，”主教练John Schneider说。“我告诉他，‘哥们，今晚的比赛才是最重要的。别担心。’今天他打出关键一棒，非常合适。”
那次道歉还包括给Schneider一个大大的拥抱，Lukes的队友们也感受到了。
“有几个队友走过来对我说，我今晚会打出关键表现来弥补这件事，”Lukes说。“我想如果你直接把球轰出墙，就不可能把跑垒搞砸了。所以这太棒了。”
Lukes在第四局下半轰出一记三分本垒打，在比赛早些时候错失一些机会后，终于让进攻有所突破。这正是Lukes非常擅长处理的球路，一个低角度变化球，他压低重心用腿发力打出。
如今一切已经平衡，我们可以重新将Lukes视为他真实的球员身份——这支球队中宝贵的一员。本赛季面对左投对Lukes来说十分艰难，但他面对右投表现很好，在接下来对阵几乎所有右投的比赛中，他应该仍会出现在阵容中。
2. Chad Dallas的关键投球与出色表现
蓝鸟在第三局满垒、两出局，老将Salvador Perez站上打击区时，换上了Chad Dallas。毫无压力。
Dallas三振了Perez，化解了危机，其中包括几次相差甚远的挥空。这名右投手为蓝鸟贡献了2 2/3局完美的后援投球，送出4次三振，将这场牛棚大战支撑到中段。
“我喜欢他的气质，也喜欢他的投球内容，”Schneider说。“他清楚地知道自己什么时候上场，并且投出了关键球。那是一次重要的三振。那是Chad表现最好的一次。他做到了我们需要他做的。”
这是Dallas在大联盟迄今最出色的时刻。令人惊讶的是，这竟然只是他在2026年为蓝鸟出场的第四次，想想他多次往返于3A水牛城，但现在感觉他会留下来，尤其是下周阵容将从26人扩大到28人。他多局投球的能力目前极为宝贵，尤其当Spencer Arrighetti仍在拉长投球局数，而蓝鸟等待Jameson Taillon回归填补第五号先发位置。
3. Sean Keys是提升阵容的选择吗？
排名第6的潜力新秀Sean Keys本赛季早前在大联盟的12场比赛中贡献不多，但他回到3A水牛城之后的表现可能很快为他赢得再次考察的机会。
Keys本赛季目前共打出28支本垒打，他在野牛队状态火热。再说一次，阵容即将扩大，为什么不在任何可能的地方寻求一些额外火力呢？
“他现在显然处于非常好的状态，”Schneider说。“我们讨论过他以及他的进攻特点，防守上如何适配。我们会继续讨论。未来一周他会在3A比赛中打一些外野。”
Keys从未打过外野，但预计很快会获得一些左外野出场机会。近年来，这支球队并不回避这种情况，愿意让火热的击球手改守新位置，只要能让他们进入阵容。本赛季进行到目前阶段，蓝鸟需要追求上限，风险之后再担心。

items.titleEn: These are the hottest hitting prospects right now -- one for each club
bodyEn: The dog days of summer have been known to wilt many a young player over the years. But in the case of the 30 hitting prospects listed below, they’re as hot as the temps have been.

These are the hottest hitters over the past month for each organization, a list that’s highlighted by 12 members of our Top 100 Prospects list. And there are three brand new professionals making the list, courtesy of the 2026 Draft as well.
Jump to: AL East | AL Central | AL West | NL East | NL Central | NL West
AMERICAN LEAGUE EAST

Blue Jays: Sean Keys, 1B/3B (No. 6)The 2024 fourth-rounder is playing like someone who really wants to return to the bigs before the year is out. Keys is hitting .351/.463/.675 with six homers and 13 walks through 20 games with Triple-A Buffalo in August. That’s a significant turnaround considering he went 4-for-30 (.133) with 10 strikeouts and no extra-base hits in his first nine games back with the Bisons after being optioned on July 23. While Keys’ power has been his biggest driver in 2026 with 27 Minor League homers total on the season, he’s also cut his whiff rate to 22.7 percent in August, the lowest mark he’s had in a month in Triple-A yet.

Orioles: Enddy Azocar, OF (No. 9)Azocar was white-hot (.552/.581/1.024) in the days just ahead of him being traded from the Red Sox to the Orioles in the Adley Rutschman trade. He’s cooled off by comparison, but has still managed to slash .356/.400/.616 with High-A Frederick since the deal. That’s an OPS of 1.185 over the last 30 days with 19 extra-base hits, helping him sit in a tie for third among all Minor League hitters with 62 XBH for the season.

Rays: Caden Bodine, C (No. 3/MLB No. 51)Bodine’s rocket rise through the Tampa Bay system continued Tuesday with his promotion to Triple-A Durham for his fourth level of the year, and no one could argue it wasn’t well-deserved. The Coastal Carolina product, who was acquired from the Orioles in last offseason’s Shane Baz deal, hit .330/.403/.462 with four homers, two doubles and an 8/14 K/BB ratio over his final 25 games with Double-A Montgomery. His 6.0 percent strikeout rate on the season is lowest among all full-season qualifiers, while his .343 average ranks second in that group of 756.

Red Sox: Franklin Primera, C/1B (No. 4)Primera has posted an OPS above 1.000 in three of his four months this season, and before August, the last time he did was June (1.355) when he was promoted from the Florida Complex League to Single-A Salem at the end of the month. The 19-year-old backstop has certainly caught up to the quality of the Carolina League with a .403/.560/.661 line, three homers and 7/15 K/BB ratio over 18 games with the RidgeYaks. His 1.45 BB/K ratio on the season ranks sixth among all MiLB qualifiers.

Yankees: Yostin Pena, OF (Not ranked among Top 30)At 18 years old, Pena was a bit on the older side for the Dominican Summer League, where he opened the season, but on July 28, he skipped the FCL to get a promotion to Single-A Tampa and hasn’t looked back since. The 6-foot-4 right-handed slugger has hit .358/.389/.597 with four homers in his first 15 games with the Tarpons. (Three of those four dingers have come in the last week alone.) His big-time power (113.6 mph max exit velocity, 108.2 90th-percentile EV in the FSL) is his most intriguing asset, though a high chase rate brings some cause for concern as he sees more full-season pitching.
AMERICAN LEAGUE CENTRAL

Guardians: Ralphy Velazquez, 1B/OF (No. 2/MLB No. 32)Velazquez clubbed 16 homers for Triple-A Columbus over a 20-game stretch from July 28 to Aug. 22. He struck out only 15 times in the same span. The only Major Leaguers to homer that many times over a similar sample size are Albert Belle, Barry Bonds, Sammy Sosa, Mark McGwire and Kyle Schwarber – a real who’s who of all-time sluggers. No other Minor Leaguer hit more than 11 dingers over the same stretch. The 21-year-old is up to a career high 27 homers on the season between Double-A and Triple-A, and with Cleveland in the thick of the AL Central and Wild Card races, his name will come up a ton in promotion discussions over the final weeks of 2026.

Royals: Jaider Suárez, SS (No. 18)Angeibel Gomez has gotten a lot of deserved praise for his introduction to pro ball in the Dominican Summer League this year, but don’t overlook Suárez who signed for $1,647,500 in January and has similarly posted impressive numbers, especially at the end of the regular season. The right-handed-hitting shortstop went 12-for-24 (.500) with five extra-base hits, seven steals, seven walks and (get this) only one strikeout over the final eight regular-season games with DSL Royals Fortuna. He didn’t quite find the same success in DSL Cup play (fanning four times in his final four postseason games), but even so, he finished 2026 with a .379/.508/.564 line and 29/35 K/BB ratio over 43 contests.

Tigers: Bryce Rainer, SS (No. 3/MLB No. 48)Rainer’s swing-and-miss issues continue to temper what could be a truly exciting profile, but there’s no doubting that this has been his best slugging month yet in his age-20 season. The left-handed-hitting shortstop went deep six times over seven games for High-A West Michigan from Aug. 14-22, and he’s hitting .282/.358/.634 with seven homers total in 17 games this month. If he can close some of the holes in his swing in his 20s, he has massive upside on both sides of the ball to become Detroit’s future at the six.

Twins: Walker Jenkins, OF (No. 1/MLB No. 15)Whenever he’s on the field and healthy, he produces, but he’s yet to play in over 100 games in a season. This year has been no different, with a shoulder sprain sidelining him for more than a month. He’s been making up for it since, hitting .368/.466/.678 with seven homers over the last month. That stretch includes a pair of two-homer games last week, adding to him knocking on the big league door even more loudly. Could that door be opened with the latest Byron Buxton injury?

White Sox: Caleb Bonemer, 3B/SS (No.2 /MLB No. 30**)**It’s been a big week for Bonemer news with Scott Merkin reporting that the Chicago prospect will start folding in center field to his defensive work before heading to the Arizona Fall League in a few weeks. His bat continues to be the most enticing part of the profile anyways, as he proved Tuesday by going 3-for-3 with a homer, two doubles and two walks for Double-A Birmingham. Since July 29, he is hitting .275/.412/.714 with 10 homers in his last 24 games in the Southern League, and his 34 dingers on the season between High-A and Double-A are tied for fourth-most in the Minors.
AMERICAN LEAGUE WEST

Angels: Jake Munroe, 3B (No. 20)The Angels’ fourth-round pick out of Louisville in 2025, Munroe has used his excellent feel to hit his way to Double-A in his first full season. He’s swinging it particularly well of late, with a .944 OPS over the last month with Rocket City. He’s continued a season-long trend of limiting strikeouts (16.6 percent for the year) and drawing walks (12.6 pct), leading to him leading all Angels Minor Leaguers with a 140 wRC+ in 2026.

Astros: Logan Hughes, OF (No. 3)The 17th pick in this year’s Draft has the longest active hitting streak in the Carolina League at 13 games, which is notable since he’s only played 13 games for Single-A Fayetteville. The Texas Tech product has opened his career with a .352/.462/.648 line, two homers and eight walks in that span, leading to a 191 wRC+ over the small sample. With Hughes’ defense drawing questions, he’ll need to hit to hold high value in the Houston system, and he’s checking that box early.

A’s: Drew Burress, OF (No. 2/MLB No. 41)Thought to be one of the members of the 2026 Draft class who could move quickly through the Minors, especially since the A’s don’t hesitate to push college bats rapidly up the ladder, Burress has put his best foot forward during his summer debut. The Georgia Tech outfielder has swung and missed a bunch (25.9 percent K rate), but offset that with a 19.8 percent BB rate while smashing six homers and slashing .306/.469/.694 with Single-A Stockton over 17 games since signing.

Mariners: Boston Smith, C/OF (No. 13)Smith hasn’t let being traded slow him down this past month. Actually, he’s been traded twice, going from the Nationals to the Rays at the end of Spring Training, then from the Rays to the Mariners in the Luis Castillo deal at the Deadline. He’s hit eight homers in 18 games since the trade, a continuation of strong performances when he was still in Tampa’s organization, leading to a .309/.434/.704 line over the last 30 days. He’s one of a dozen Minor League hitters with 30 or more homers for the season.

Rangers: Dylan Dreiling, OF (No. 13)This is the second time Dreiling has made our hot hitters list – he was the Rangers’ entry in April as well – and for good reason. The left-handed hitting outfielder slashed .395/.454/.709 with 13 extra-base hits (seven homers) over the past month. He has a .915 OPS for the season now, good for fourth in the Double-A Texas League, and he’s also tied for fourth with 45 extra-base hits.
NATIONAL LEAGUE EAST

Braves: Connor Essenburg, OF (No. 11)Essenburg got super hot at the end of July with Single-A Augusta, hitting .579/.667/1.474 over his last 27 plate appearances to earn a bump up to High-A Rome. He’s still adjusting to the new level, but his overall numbers for the past month still jump off the page, as the 19-year-old outfielder has a combined 1.053 OPS with 11 extra-base hits and more walks than strikeouts in that time span. This stretch has allowed him to vault into the organizational lead with 144 wRC+ for the season.

Marlins: Brandon Compton, OF (No. 13)The Marlins’ second-round pick in 2025, Compton scuffled in April and May with High-A Beloit, but started figuring things out in June and kept on raking with a promotion to Double-A at the end of that month. He hasn’t stopped since, including a .357/.442/.816 line over the last 30 days, a stretch that’s included 10 homers and 13 doubles. His 32 home runs for the season put him in a tie for seventh among all Minor Leaguers and he tops Marlins farmhands with his 164 wRC+.

Mets: Aidan Smith, OF (No. 16)Smith faced major hit-tool questions when he came over from the Rays system in the Freddy Peralta Deadline deal after hitting .215/.283/.410 with a 32.0 K% over 49 games with High-A Bowling Green. To be clear, those issues do still exist. But he’s also taken his walks and produced much more thump with Brooklyn following his move to the Mets. Through 16 games with New York’s High-A affiliate, Smith is hitting .333/.446/.617 with five homers and a 174 wRC+. He has a solid power-speed combination and provides defensive value up the middle, so if he can keep the hit tool at even just a 40 on the 20-80 scale, that’d be a nice get for the Mets.

Nationals: Seaver King, SS (No. 4/MLB No. 71)Known as a hit-over-power shortstop, King has flipped a power switch in August shortly after recovering from an oblique injury. From Aug. 8-20 with Triple-A Rochester, he went deep eight times over an 11-game span, hitting .489/.547/1.043 across 53 plate appearances in that time. His 1.228 OPS in August ranks third-best in the International League this month behind Velazquez’s 1.424 and Jenkins’ 1.256. He made his first Minor League start at third base on Aug. 19, but if the Nationals are serious about moving CJ Abrams to second base before the year is out, King could be the one to slot in at shortstop in an MLB debut soon.

Phillies: Francisco Renteria, OF (No. 3/MLB No. 81)We know we need to take DSL stats with a grain of salt, but it’s hard not to get excited about Renteria and what he’s done in his pro debut after signing with the Phillies for $4 million in January. This past month has been more of the same, with a .377/.482/.797 line, more walks than strikeouts, 15 extra-base hits (six homers) and 10 steals. That includes going 4-for-11 with a homer and three steals over three playoff games. An 1.152 OPS with 11 homers and 24 steals over 53 games is a very good way to make a first impression.
NATIONAL LEAGUE CENTRAL

Brewers: Brailyn Antunez (No. 29)Antunez was a solid performer in the Arizona Complex League to begin his age-18 season but struck out 31.3 percent of the time, heightening concerns about his hit tool as he moved stateside. Not only is he making more contact since his arrival at Single-A Wilson on July 26, but he’s also performing better across the board as a hitter with a .391/.495/.696 line and seven homers in 24 games in the Carolina League. That’s a 206 wRC+ across 112 plate appearances, aided by improved contact rates and an increase in line drives from his right-handed bat.

Cardinals: Rainiel Rodriguez, C/1B (No. 1/MLB No. 18)Rodriguez homered twice for the second straight game Tuesday night, and even that just felt like more of the same from the right-handed-hitting backstop. Since July 26, he’s hitting .462/.495/.934 with 10 homers, 13 doubles and only nine strikeouts over 22 games (101 plate appearances). That’s right, he has more than double the amount of extra-base hits as K’s in this recent run. His 19 homers total with Springfield are the most in a single season by a Double-A catcher aged 19 or younger since 2006, beating out Samuel Basallo’s 16 in second place, and his 149 wRC+ ranks only second behind Mike Trout’s 162 in 2011 at the same level and age group.

Cubs: Kane Kepley, OF (No. 5)The Cubs’ second-rounder a year ago has hit his way from High-A to Double-A in his first full season, a promotion that happened during this past 30-day stretch. He hasn’t missed a beat, with a 1.076 combined OPS during the time period. It includes 10 extra-base hits (five homers), more walks than strikeouts (25-15) and going a perfect 14-for-14 in stolen base attempts. His 61 steals (in 66 attempts) puts him in a tie for third among all Minor League speedsters.

Pirates: Tony Blanco Jr., 1B (No. 27)There might not be anyone in the Minors with more raw power than the 6-foot-7 Blanco, but he’s had trouble staying healthy enough to get in a rhythm to get to it consistently. His 75 games played this year are by far a career high, and he missed time with a hamstring issue. Regular playing time has allowed him to find the seats and he hit 10 homers last month (12.2 pct HR rate) to finish with a 1.256 OPS. He finished last week with back-to-back two-homer games to give him 23 for the year. That’s good for fourth in the South Atlantic league despite having played only 71 games with Greensboro to date.

Reds: Justin Lebron, SS (No. 3)Lebron arguably had the best set of overall raw tools in the 2026 Draft class, but his struggles in his junior season with Alabama, particularly in the SEC, led to him lasting until the Reds picked at No. 18 overall. It’s a super small sample size – 12 games and 50 at-bats – but his .320/.370/.700 line in that span could provide a nice foundation to build from. The K’s are a bit high (25.9 pct), but he’s collected nine extra-base hits (five homers) with High-A Dayton.
NATIONAL LEAGUE WEST

D-backs: Carlos Virahonda (No. 5)Virahonda was already known as an above-average defender behind the plate with a plus arm coming into the year, and his offensive surge has fueled his rise into the Top 5 of the Arizona rankings. Now with High-A Hillsboro, the 20-year-old backstop has reached base in 18 straight games with a .385/.500/.600 line, three homers and an even 10/10 K/BB ratio over that span. His 18 homers on the season are a significant bump up from his previous career high of four set last season.

Dodgers: Josue De Paula, OF (No. 1/MLB No. 6)The Dodgers’ top prospect, and the only top 10 overall guy to make the list this time around, De Paula has had a terrific season with Double-A Tulsa. He’s second in the Texas League with his .996 OPS and currently has 25 homers and 29 steals. This past month certainly hasn’t hurt, as the 21-year-old outfielder has posted a .322/.426/.678 line with nine homers in 108 plate appearances.

Giants: Josuar Gonzalez, SS/2B (No. 1/MLB No. 17)The 18-year-old infielder began this year in the Arizona Complex League, but quickly earned a jump to full-season ball in late July. He shows no signs of slowing down, slashing .360/.463/.584 over the last month with Single-A San Jose, a stretch that includes 11 extra-base hits and seven steals. He’s played 52 total games to date this season, with an OPS over 1.000 and a 151 wRC+.

Padres: Ethan Salas, C (No. 1/MLB No. 23)Though he’s gone a little cold the last three games, Salas showed he didn’t need much time to catch up to the Triple-A-quality pitching after his El Paso debut on July 29. He’s hit .303/.382/.526 with three homers, 11 walks and nine strikeouts in 20 games with the Chihuahuas, and his 114 wRC+ is slightly higher than the 111 mark he put up over 72 games with Double-A San Antonio to begin his age-20 season. His best skill at the Minors’ top level has been making contact in the zone, backed by good swing decisions, and that, along with his defense, could help him push for an MLB debut before the season is up.

Rockies: Zac Veen, OF (No. 11)Are the Rockies finally getting the player they hoped they were acquiring when they took Veen No. 9 overall in the 2020 Draft? That might be TBD as he’s still figuring out Major League pitching, but this season – and this past month in particular – in Triple-A has been very encouraging. Veen slashed .436/.515/1.055 with eight homers in his last 64 Minor League plate appearances before getting called back up to the big leagues, and he has homered twice in 10 games there. For the season with Albuquerque, Veen leads the Pacific Coast League in OPS (1.037), XBH (65) and total bases (249).
items.titleZh: 各队当前最火热的打击新秀
items.summaryZh: 盘点MLB各队近一个月最火热的打击新秀，包括12位百大新秀和3位2026届新秀，蓝鸟Sean Keys在列。
bodyZh: 炎炎夏日通常会让许多年轻球员状态下滑。但对于下面列出的30位打击新秀来说，他们却和气温一样火热。
以下是每支球队近一个月最火热的打击者，名单中有12位来自我们的百大新秀榜单。此外，还有三位2026年选秀刚签下的职业新秀入选。
跳转至：美联东区 | 美联中区 | 美联西区 | 国联东区 | 国联中区 | 国联西区
美国联盟东区

蓝鸟：Sean Keys，一垒手/三垒手（队内第6新秀）。这位2024年第四轮选中的球员，表现得像是真的想在年底前重返大联盟。8月份，他在3A布法罗的20场比赛中打击率为.351/.463/.675，轰出6发本垒打，选到13次保送。考虑到他在7月23日被下放后，回到野牛队的前9场比赛30打数仅4安打（.133），吞下10次三振且没有长打，这是一个显著的转折。尽管Keys在2026赛季的主要动力是他的长打能力，他本赛季小联盟合计27发本垒打，但他在8月也将挥空率降至22.7%，这是他升上3A以来单月最低。
金莺：Enddy Azocar，外野手（队内第9新秀）。在Adley Rutschman交易中从红袜被送到金莺之前，Azocar状态火热（.552/.581/1.024）。相比之下他有所降温，但交易后在高阶1A弗雷德里克仍缴出.356/.400/.616的打击三围。最近30天他的OPS高达1.185，并贡献19支长打，帮助他以62支长打与所有小联盟打者并列第三。

光芒：Caden Bodine，捕手（队内第3/MLB第51新秀）。Bodine在坦帕湾体系的火箭式上升周二继续，他被升上3A达勒姆，这是他本赛季第四个级别，没有人能说这不是实至名归。这位来自卡罗莱纳海岸的球员，在去年休赛期Shane Baz交易中从金莺获得，他在2A蒙哥马利的最后25场比赛中打出.330/.403/.462，有4发本垒打、2支二垒安打和8/14的三振保送比。他本赛季6.0%的三振率是所有满赛季资格打者中最低的，而他的.343打击率在这756人中排名第二。

红袜：Franklin Primera，捕手/一垒手（队内第4新秀）。本赛季四个月中，Primera有三个月的OPS超过1.000，在8月之前，他上一次做到是在6月（1.355），当时他在月底从佛罗里达综合联盟升上1A塞勒姆。这位19岁捕手已经跟上了卡罗莱纳联盟的投球水准，在为RidgeYaks出战的18场比赛中，缴出.403/.560/.661的打击三围，3发本垒打和7/15的三振保送比。他本赛季1.45的保送/三振比在所有小联盟合格打者中排名第六。

洋基：Yostin Pena，外野手（未进入前30新秀榜）。18岁的Pena在本赛季开始的多米尼加夏季联赛中年龄稍大，但在7月28日，他跳过佛罗里达综合联盟直接升上1A坦帕，自此便一路向前。这位6英尺4英寸的右打重炮手在Tarpons的前15场比赛中打出.358/.389/.597，并有4发本垒打。（其中3发是在最近一周打出的。）他强大的长打火力（在佛罗里达州立联盟中最大出口速度113.6英里/小时，90分位出口速度108.2）是他最吸引人的资产，不过随着他面对更多全赛季投手，较高的追打率也令人担忧。
美国联盟中区

守护者：Ralphy Velazquez，一垒手/外野手（队内第2/MLB第32新秀）。7月28日至8月22日期间，Velazquez在3A哥伦布的20场比赛中轰出16发本垒打，期间仅被三振15次。在类似的小样本中，只有Albert Belle、Barry Bonds、Sammy Sosa、Mark McGwire和Kyle Schwarber做到过这么多本垒打——这真是历史级重炮手的名单。同期没有其他小联盟球员打出超过11发本垒打。这位21岁球员本赛季在2A和3A合计轰出生涯新高的27发本垒打，而克利夫兰正在美联中区和外卡竞争中激战，他的名字将在2026年最后几周频繁出现在升班讨论中。

皇家：Jaider Suárez，游击手（队内第18新秀）。Angeibel Gomez今年在多米尼加夏季联赛的职业首秀中获得了许多应得的赞誉，但不要忽视Suárez，他在一月以1,647,500美元签约，同样打出了亮眼数据，尤其是在常规赛末段。这位右打游击手在DSL Fortuna的最后八场常规赛中，24个打数打出12支安打（.500），有5支长打、7次盗垒、7次保送，而且（注意）只有1次三振。他在DSL杯赛表现不佳（最后四场季后赛中吞下4次三振），但即便如此，他在43场比赛中以.379/.508/.564的打击三围和29/35的三振保送比结束了2026赛季。

老虎：Bryce Rainer，游击手（队内第3/MLB第48新秀）。Rainer的挥空问题继续限制着他本可以极其亮眼的潜力，但毫无疑问，这是他在20岁时表现最好的一个长打月份。这位左打游击手在8月14日至22日为高阶1A西密歇根出战的七场比赛中轰出六发本垒打，本月17场比赛中合计打击率为.282/.358/.634，有七发本垒打。如果他在20多岁时能封堵挥棒中的漏洞，他在攻防两端都有巨大的上升空间，成为底特律未来的游击手。
双城：Walker Jenkins，外野手（队内第1/MLB第15新秀）。只要他健康上场，就能有所产出，但他还没有单赛季出场超过100场。今年也不例外，肩部扭伤让他缺阵超过一个月。此后他一直在弥补，最近一个月打击率为.368/.466/.678，轰出7发本垒打。这段时间包括上周的两次单场双响炮，让他敲大联盟大门的声音更响亮了。随着Byron Buxton最新一次受伤，这扇门会被打开吗？

白袜：Caleb Bonemer，三垒手/游击手（队内第2/MLB第30新秀）。对Bonemer来说这是重要的一周，Scott Merkin报道称，这位芝加哥新秀将在几周后前往亚利桑那秋季联盟之前，开始把中外野纳入他的防守工作。无论如何，他的球棒仍是其球探报告中最诱人的部分，正如他周二在2A伯明翰4个打数3安打、一轰、两支二垒安打和两次保送所证明的那样。自7月29日以来，他在南方联盟的最近24场比赛中打击率为.275/.412/.714，轰出10发本垒打，而他本赛季在高阶1A和2A合计34发本垒打，与小联盟第四多并列。
美国联盟西区
天使：Jake Munroe，三垒手（队内第20新秀）。天使在2025年第四轮从路易斯维尔选中的Munroe，凭借出色的打击感觉，在首个完整赛季就打到了2A。他最近状态尤其出色，过去一个月在Rocket City的OPS为.944。他延续了本赛季控制三振（全年16.6%）和选保送（12.6%）的趋势，以140 wRC+领先所有天使小联盟球员。

太空人：Logan Hughes，外野手（队内第3新秀）。今年选秀的第17顺位目前保持着卡罗莱纳联盟最长的连续安打场次——13场，值得注意的是他仅为1A费耶特维尔出战了13场比赛。这位德州理工出身的球员职业生涯开局在13场比赛中缴出.352/.462/.648的打击三围，2发本垒打和8次保送，在小样本中wRC+高达191。由于Hughes的防守受到质疑，他需要在休斯顿体系中靠打击保持高价值，而他已经早早做到了这一点。
运动家：Drew Burress，外野手（队内第2/MLB第41新秀）。作为2026届选秀中被认为能快速升上小联盟的成员之一，尤其是运动家从不犹豫让大学打者快速升级，Burress在夏季首秀中展现出了最佳状态。这位佐治亚理工外野手挥空不少（25.9%的三振率），但以19.8%的保送率抵消了这一点，同时自签约以来为1A斯托克顿出战17场，轰出6发本垒打，打击三围为.306/.469/.694。

水手：Boston Smith，捕手/外野手（队内第13新秀）。过去一个月，Smith并没有因为被交易而放慢脚步。实际上，他被交易了两次：春训结束时从国民到光芒，然后在交易截止日Luis Castillo交易中从光芒到水手。自交易以来，他在18场比赛中轰出8发本垒打，延续了他在光芒体系时的强劲表现，过去30天打击三围为.309/.434/.704。他是本赛季小联盟中12位轰出30发以上本垒打的打者之一。
游骑兵：Dylan Dreiling，外野手（队内第13新秀）。这是Dreiling第二次入选我们的火热打者名单——他也是游骑兵4月的代表——原因充分。这位左打外野手过去一个月打击三围为.395/.454/.709，有13支长打（7发本垒打）。他本赛季OPS为.915，在2A得州联盟排名第四，同时以45支长打并列第四。
国家联盟东区
勇士：Connor Essenburg，外野手（队内第11新秀）。Essenburg在7月底为1A奥古斯塔效力时状态火爆，在最后27个打席中打出.579/.667/1.474，从而升上高阶1A罗马。他仍在适应新级别，但他过去一个月的整体数据依然令人瞩目，这位19岁外野手在此期间合计OPS为1.053，有11支长打，保送多于三振。这一波表现让他以144 wRC+跃居球队小联盟之首。
马林鱼：Brandon Compton，外野手（队内第13新秀）。马林鱼2025年的二轮秀Compton在4月和5月于高阶1A贝洛伊特表现挣扎，但6月开始找到状态，并在月底升上2A后持续打击火热。此后他从未停歇，最近30天打击三围为.357/.442/.816，包括10发本垒打和13支二垒安打。他赛季32发本垒打使他在所有小联盟球员中并列第七，并以164 wRC+领跑马林鱼农场球员。

大都会：Aidan Smith，外野手（队内第16新秀）。在Freddy Peralta交易截止日交易中从光芒体系来到大都会之前，Smith在高阶1A鲍灵格林49场比赛中打击率为.215/.283/.410，三振率32.0%，因此他的打击能力受到重大质疑。需要说明的是，这些问题仍然存在。但在加盟大都会后，他在布鲁克林选到保送并产生了更大的长打火力。在为纽约高阶1A球队出战的16场比赛中，Smith打击率为.333/.446/.617，有5发本垒打和174 wRC+。他具备不错的力量与速度结合，并能提供中外野防守价值，因此如果他的打击能力哪怕只能保持在20-80量表上的40分，对大都会来说也是一笔不错的收获。

国民：Seaver King，游击手（队内第4/MLB第71新秀）。King以打击优先于力量的游击手著称，但在8月从斜肌伤势康复后，他开启了力量开关。8月8日至20日为3A罗切斯特出战的11场比赛中，他轰出8发本垒打，期间53个打席中打出.489/.547/1.043。他8月的OPS为1.228，在当月国际联盟中排名第三，仅次于Velazquez的1.424和Jenkins的1.256。8月19日他职业生涯首次在小联盟比赛中担任三垒手，但如果国民真的打算在年底前将CJ Abrams移至二垒，King可能会很快在大联盟首秀中填补游击手位置。

费城人：Francisco Renteria，外野手（队内第3/MLB第81新秀）。我们知道需要对DSL数据持保留态度，但很难不对Renteria在一月以400万美元签约费城人后的职业首秀所做出的表现感到兴奋。过去一个月依然如此，他打出.377/.482/.797的打击三围，保送多于三振，有15支长打（6发本垒打）和10次盗垒。其中包括在三场季后赛中11个打数4安打、1轰和3盗。在53场比赛中缴出1.152 OPS、11发本垒打和24次盗垒，这是留下第一印象的绝佳方式。
国家联盟中区

酿酒人：Brailyn Antunez（队内第29新秀）。Antunez在亚利桑那综合联盟开启18岁赛季时表现稳定，但三振率高达31.3%，这让人们对他转战美国本土后的打击能力更加担忧。自7月26日抵达1A威尔逊后，他不仅打出了更多接触，而且整体打击表现更上一层楼，在卡罗莱纳联盟的24场比赛中打出.391/.495/.696，并有7发本垒打。在112个打席中wRC+高达206，这得益于更高的接触率和来自右打的更多平飞球。

红雀：Rainiel Rodriguez，捕手/一垒手（队内第1/MLB第18新秀）。周二晚，Rodriguez连续第二场单场双响炮，即便这对他来说也只是常规操作。自7月26日以来，他在22场比赛（101个打席）中打出.462/.495/.934，有10发本垒打、13支二垒安打，仅9次三振。没错，在这波表现中他的长打数量是三振数的两倍多。他在斯普林菲尔德总计19发本垒打，是自2006年以来2A捕手在19岁或以下单赛季最多，超过排名第二的Samuel Basallo的16发，而他的149 wRC+仅次于2011年同期同级别的Mike Trout的162。
小熊：Kane Kepley，外野手（队内第5新秀）。小熊一年前的二轮秀在首个完整赛季中从高阶1A打到2A，这次升班发生在过去30天内。他完全没有掉链子，期间合计OPS为1.076。包括10支长打（5发本垒打）、保送多于三振（25-15），以及盗垒尝试14次全部成功。他本赛季61次盗垒（66次尝试）在所有小联盟快腿中并列第三。

海盗：Tony Blanco Jr.，一垒手（队内第27新秀）。在小联盟中，可能没有谁的原始力量能比得上6英尺7英寸的Blanco，但他一直难以保持健康以进入节奏并持续发挥。他今年出战75场，是生涯最高，而且他还因腿筋问题缺阵。稳定的出场时间让他能够把球轰出围墙，他上个月打出10发本垒打（12.2%的本垒打率），最终OPS为1.256。上周他以连续两场双响炮收官，赛季本垒打数来到23发。尽管目前只为格林斯伯勒出战71场，这已在南大西洋联盟排名第四。

红人：Justin Lebron，游击手（队内第3新秀）。Lebron可以说是2026届选秀中整体原始天赋最全面的球员之一，但他在阿拉巴马大学大三赛季的挣扎，尤其是在SEC联盟中的表现，使他一直掉到红人用第18顺位选中。这是一个超小样本——12场比赛50个打席——但他在此期间打出.320/.370/.700的打击三围，可以打下不错的基础。三振率略高（25.9%），但他为高阶1A代顿贡献了9支长打（5发本垒打）。
国家联盟西区
响尾蛇：Carlos Virahonda（队内第5新秀）。Virahonda在年初就已是一名高于平均水平的捕手防守者，拥有加强的臂力，而他的进攻爆发也推动他升至亚利桑那新秀榜前五。如今在高阶1A希尔斯伯勒，这位20岁捕手连续18场上垒，期间打出.385/.500/.600的打击三围、3发本垒打和10/10的三振保送比。他赛季18发本垒打，比上赛季创下的生涯最高4发有了显著提升。
道奇：Josue De Paula，外野手（队内第1/MLB第6新秀）。道奇的头号新秀，也是本次唯一进入榜单的前十新秀，De Paula在2A塔尔萨度过了出色的赛季。他以.996的OPS在得州联盟排名第二，目前有25发本垒打和29次盗垒。过去一个月当然也没有拖后腿，这位21岁外野手在108个打席中打出.322/.426/.678，并有9发本垒打。
巨人：Josuar Gonzalez，游击手/二垒手（队内第1/MLB第17新秀）。这位18岁内野手今年从亚利桑那综合联盟起步，但在7月底迅速升上全赛季联赛。他没有减速的迹象，过去一个月为1A圣何塞打出.360/.463/.584的打击三围，包括11支长打和7次盗垒。他本赛季至今共出场52场，OPS超过1.000，wRC+为151。

教士：Ethan Salas，捕手（队内第1/MLB第23新秀）。尽管最近三场比赛状态有些下滑，但Salas在7月29日于埃尔帕索首秀后，展现了他并不需要太多时间来适应3A级别的投球。他为Chihuahuas出战的20场比赛中，打击率为.303/.382/.526，有3发本垒打、11次保送和9次三振，他的114 wRC+略高于他20岁赛季初在2A圣安东尼奥72场比赛的111。他在小联盟最高级别的最强技能是打击好球带内的球，加上良好的挥棒决策，再加上他的防守，这可以帮助他在本赛季结束前争取大联盟首秀。

洛矶：Zac Veen，外野手（队内第11新秀）。洛矶终于得到了他们在2020年选秀第9顺位选中Veen时所希望得到的球员吗？这可能仍有待观察，因为他还在摸索大联盟投球，但本赛季——尤其是过去一个月——在3A的表现非常令人鼓舞。在被重新叫回大联盟前，Veen在最近64个小联盟打席中打出.436/.515/1.055，并有8发本垒打，回到大联盟后10场比赛中也轰出2发。本赛季在阿尔伯克基，Veen在太平洋海岸联盟的OPS（1.037）、长打数（65）和总垒打数（249）方面均领跑。
